tasks.task:
The wire protocol package (packages/wire) is the single shared contract every other package imports. It must define and validate every event type in the system as a discriminated union with runtime zod schemas.

Verify that the current packages/wire implementation covers all of the following and repair or reimplement anything missing, wrong, or untested:

Session events (daemon → server → surfaces): chat.spawned {chatId, folder, parentChatId?}, chat.message {chatId, role, content, seq}, chat.tool_call {chatId, tool, args, seq}, chat.tool_result {chatId, tool, result, seq}, chat.permission_request {chatId, request, seq}, chat.state {chatId, activity, lastUpdated} where activity is exactly the union idle|running|awaiting-permission|errored, chat.stopped {chatId, reason}, chat.error {chatId, error, seq}, daemon.online {}, daemon.offline {}, daemon.unauthenticated {reason}.

Surface events (surface → server → daemon): chat.input {chatId, message, localId} where localId is a UUID for dedup, chat.permission_response {requestId, approve}, chat.spawn_request {folder, prompt?, parentChatId?}, chat.stop_request {chatId}, chat.resume_request {chatId}, chat.focus_change {chatId}, file.write {chatId, path, content}, surface.heartbeat {}, surface.foregrounded {}, surface.backgrounded {}.

Cross-chat tool events: patch.peek.request {sourceChatId, targetChatId}, patch.peek.response {sourceChatId, targetChatId, state}, patch.send_to {sourceChatId, targetChatId, message}, patch.spawn {sourceChatId, folder, prompt}.

Notification event: notify {chatId, channel, message, priority?} where channel is exactly push|desktop|telegram|speakers.

Control events: hello {clientType, clientVersion, auth}, ack {seq}, chat.replay {chatId, fromSeq}.

Audio protocol types: AudioSurfaceKind must include 'device' in addition to any other values. The voice token, session start, and audio frame types used by voice surfaces and the voice device must be defined.

Every event that represents a chat stream item must carry a seq field of type number. chat.input must carry a localId field. The package must have zero runtime dependencies beyond zod. All types must be exported so server, daemon, CLI, web, and mobile can import them.

Run unit tests to prove each event type parses correctly and rejects invalid payloads. Any event type that lacks test coverage must be tested. Any schema mismatch with the spec must be fixed.

The auth package (packages/auth) provides all cryptographic identity operations used across the system. It must be the single place Ed25519 keypair operations, EdDSA-JWT minting, JWT verification, and QR-code pairing nonce generation live.

Verify and repair: Ed25519 keypair generation produces a valid keypair stored as the user's stable account identity. EdDSA-JWT minting signs a bearer token with the user's private key in RFC 8037 format. JWT verification checks a token against the stored Ed25519 public key and rejects tokens with invalid signatures, wrong key, or expired claims. QR-code pairing nonce generation produces a random one-time string sufficient for a pairing round-trip. Surface credential signing: an already-linked surface can sign a subordinate credential for a new surface using its private key.

All crypto must use the @noble/ed25519 and @noble/hashes and jose libraries. node:crypto's Ed25519 path must not be used. No ANTHROPIC_API_KEY must appear anywhere in this package.

Test every operation including: correct JWT verifies, tampered JWT rejects, JWT signed by wrong key rejects, expired JWT rejects. The tests must run via vitest.

name: Server core — WebSocket hub, registry, presence, linking

tasks.task:
The server (packages/server) is the dumb relay and registry. It must route events between surfaces and the daemon, track presence, and handle device linking. It makes no LLM calls.

Verify and repair the following, testing each behaviour against a running server instance:

WebSocket endpoint GET /ws: accepts connections only from clients that send a valid EdDSA-JWT hello frame (verified via stored Ed25519 public key using jose). Rejects connections with missing, malformed, or unknown-key JWTs immediately after the hello frame. Maintains separate connection records for the daemon and for surfaces. Routes events from surfaces to the daemon and from the daemon to the correct surface(s) by (account, chatId). Emits daemon.online when the daemon's WS connects, daemon.offline when the daemon's WS drops or heartbeats timeout. Cleans up all connection state on disconnect.

Commit-before-broadcast discipline: server emits over WebSocket only after the underlying flat-file write is fsync'd. Any event dispatch that skips this is a bug — find and fix it.

Presence tracker: each surface sends surface.heartbeat every 10s. Server tracks lastHeartbeatAt per (account, surface). isActive(account) = any surface had a heartbeat within the last 30s. This value is used by notification routing.

Registry: account record (Ed25519 public key) and daemon key stored in /data/registry.json. Writes must be atomic (temp file + rename). The daemon registers once via the QR-pairing flow.

Device linking endpoint POST /auth/link: initiates the Happy-style QR pairing flow. An already-linked surface scans the QR, approves, and the server relays the new surface's credential back. The new surface stores its device credential. Any already-linked surface can revoke another from Settings — server invalidates the JWT and terminates the corresponding WebSocket.

GET /healthz returns 200.

Test: a surface with a valid JWT can connect and receive events; a surface with an invalid JWT is rejected; presence collapses after 30s of no heartbeat; daemon.online/offline events reach surfaces correctly.

steps: Boot the real server and the real daemon; let the daemon perform its real registration (Ed25519 key stored in /data/registry.json) and connect to GET /ws presenting a genuine EdDSA-JWT hello frame verified via the stored public key (jose).

Then attempt a second WS connection presenting a JWT signed by an unknown/forged key.

name: Server — jobs CRUD, cron, webhook ingress, Telegram, chat history endpoints

tasks.task:
The server handles all job management, trigger dispatch, external inbound channels, and chat history serving.

Verify and repair, testing each behaviour:

Job CRUD endpoints (GET /jobs, POST /jobs, PATCH /jobs/:id, DELETE /jobs/:id): job definitions stored at /data/jobs/<id>.json, atomic writes (fsync). GET returns all jobs. POST creates with generated ULID id. PATCH merges update. DELETE removes file. All job file writes trigger the chokidar watcher (daemon is notified separately).

In-process cron scheduler (node-cron): fires cron-trigger jobs at their UTC-scheduled times. Each tick produces {firedAt} payload and dispatches the job's action event (chat.spawn_request or chat.input) to the daemon's WebSocket, identical to a surface-originated event. If daemon is offline, action is buffered to /data/pending/<jobId>-<fireId>.jsonl and flushed on daemon reconnect. Max 100 pending per job; oldest dropped with a log line when limit exceeded.

Webhook ingress POST /api/webhooks/<jobId>: server looks up job, verifies signature per scheme (none = accept anything, hmac-sha256 = verify X-Patch-Signature header, github = X-Hub-Signature-256, stripe = Stripe signed-event scheme). Drop on mismatch. Every inbound hit appended to /data/webhooks/<jobId>.jsonl including signature failures. On pass: evaluate JSONata filter against payload (via jsonata library). Filter truthy → resolve action templates → dispatch to daemon. Filter falsy → logged as filter-rejected in /data/runs/<jobId>.jsonl. Filter error → logged as filter-error. Every fire (successful or not) appended to /data/runs/<jobId>.jsonl.

GET /api/jobs/:id/runs: returns recent entries from /data/runs/<jobId>.jsonl. GET /api/jobs/:id/webhooks: returns recent entries from /data/webhooks/<jobId>.jsonl.

Telegram webhook POST /telegram/webhook: accepts messages only from TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USER_ID (silently drop all others). Routes accepted messages to the daemon as input to the Telegram special thread.

Google OAuth redirect GET /oauth/google/callback: handles Calendar integration OAuth flow.

Chat endpoints: GET /chats returns list of all chats (read from daemon state or daemon-mediated). GET /chats/:id/history?since=<seq> returns events since the given seq for that chat.

At server startup: check that all notify channel credentials referenced in env vars (FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON or ntfy config, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN) are present and valid. If any required credential is missing, abort with a clear error message pointing to the .env key. No silent skipping.

Test: cron fires at correct UTC time and dispatches to daemon; webhook with correct signature passes and dispatches; webhook with wrong signature is dropped and logged; Telegram message from wrong user is dropped; chat history endpoint returns correct events since given seq.

name: Daemon — session lifecycle, chat_state, history, IPC

tasks.task:
The daemon (packages/daemon) owns every Claude Code session and is the source of truth for chat state. It is a single Node process. The SDK runs in-process; there are no claude subprocess spawns.

Verify and repair, testing each behaviour against a running daemon:

Startup: scans ~/.patch/chats/*/meta.json and marks all chats idle in memory. Does NOT auto-resume any chat — resume only happens on the next user message.

OAuth check: before making any SDK query(), check ~/.claude.json for a valid token. If missing or expired, emit daemon.unauthenticated on the server WebSocket and refuse to start any query until re-authenticated. Do not fall back to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY — that key must be explicitly stripped from the environment passed to every SDK query().

Spawning a chat: generate chatId as ULID. Validate the folder exists on the daemon box — error loudly if not. Call SDK query() with: cwd set to the folder, permissionMode bypassPermissions, the inline MCP server config (PATCH_CHAT_ID and PATCH_DAEMON_SOCKET in env), and resume: undefined for new chats. The SDK runs asynchronously; iterate its result stream.

Session ID capture: the SDK emits a result message containing session_id early in the stream. Daemon captures it and writes to ~/.patch/chats/<chatId>/meta.json atomically. If a chat calls /clear or /compact mid-session, the SDK emits a new session_id in the next result message — daemon updates meta.json.

Event piping: every SDK event (messages, tool calls, tool results, permission requests) must be translated into the correct wire protocol event type (using packages/wire schemas) and emitted to the server WebSocket, which relays to surfaces.

Sequence durability: per-chat monotonic sequence counter is persisted atomically to ~/.patch/chats/<chatId>/seq after every event emit. On restart, seq resumes from this persisted value so replay continues to work across crashes.

In-memory chat_state: maintain per chat: {chatId, name, activity, lastMessages (last 20), lastUpdated, folder}. Activity transitions: idle → running when query starts, running → awaiting-permission on permission_request event, awaiting-permission → running on permission_response, running → idle on query completion, any → errored on error. Rebuilt from tailing history on restart.

Daemon restart behaviour: on restart, mark all chats idle. On next user message for a chat, call SDK query() with resume: meta.claudeSessionId. If claudeSessionId is missing or invalid, mark chat errored and surface the condition — do not silently proceed.

Stopping a chat: call .close() on the SDK query iterator. Chat metadata is retained. Chat is resumable via next user message.

Loopback control IPC over Unix domain socket ~/.patch/daemon.sock: GET /list returns active chats, POST /spawn-chat spawns new chat, POST /stop-chat stops a chat, POST /stop shuts the daemon down. No auth (same host, same user).

patch daemon start/stop/status/list/clean subcommands must work correctly.

Test: spawn a chat in a valid folder → events flow to surfaces; spawn in non-existent folder → loud error; daemon restart → chat resumes from persisted session; seq is persisted and survives restart; OAuth missing → daemon.unauthenticated emitted.

name: Daemon — MCP server and all patch tools

tasks.task:
The daemon launches a stdio MCP server (patch-tools-server) as a child process for each SDK query. This child is the tool surface that every chat's Claude agent sees. It must not be registered in the global Claude Code config — it exists only for the lifetime of each query.

Verify and repair: the MCP server is built using @modelcontextprotocol/sdk. It is launched per query with PATCH_CHAT_ID and PATCH_DAEMON_SOCKET env vars. It communicates back to the daemon over the Unix domain socket at PATCH_DAEMON_SOCKET. The daemon holds all state; the MCP child is a thin wire. The chat agent does not pass its own ID — the MCP child knows it from PATCH_CHAT_ID at boot.

All of the following patch tools must be implemented and working, tested by calling them from a Claude session inside the daemon:

patch_peek(chatId, opts?): returns {chat_state, events: [...], truncated}. Default limit 50, max 200. chat_state per spec (activity, name, folder, lastUpdated, lastMessages). truncated: true if older events exist. Non-existent chatId returns an error.

patch_history(chatId, {before, limit}): paginated raw event accessor. before is an event id. Returns up to limit events older than that (limit ≤ 200 hard cap). Multiple calls handle deep history.

patch_list_chats(): returns [{chatId, folder, lastUpdated, activity}] for all known chats.

patch_send_to(chatId, message): delivers message as a user-turn into the recipient chat — the agent processes it as if the human said it. This is in-process since there is one daemon.

patch_spawn(folder, prompt?): creates a new chat in the given folder.

patch_stop(chatId): stops the given chat's SDK query.

patch_call({reason, surface?}): queues a voice call request — rings phone (FCM high-priority data message triggering ConnectionService) and desktop (window-raise + chime + banner) concurrently. First surface to accept wins, others stop. If decline or 30s timeout, falls through to push notification with reason text.

patch_notify({channel, message, priority?, deviceId?}): fires the notification routing path. channel must be one of push|desktop|telegram|speakers. deviceId only for speakers.

patch_list_devices(): returns [{deviceId, name, online, muted, lastUsedAt}] from registered voice devices.

patch_job_create, patch_job_list, patch_job_update, patch_job_delete, patch_job_enable, patch_job_disable: make authenticated HTTP calls to the server's job CRUD endpoints using the daemonKey. Return the job data.

patch_job_runs(jobId, limit?): reads /data/runs/<jobId>.jsonl. Newest-first, default 50 max 200.

patch_job_webhooks(jobId, limit?): reads /data/webhooks/<jobId>.jsonl. Newest-first, default 50 max 200.

All tools must be prefixed patch_ and must not collide with Claude Code's native tool names (CronCreate, CronList, CronDelete, Task, etc.).

Test: from inside a running chat session, call each tool and verify the correct side effect or return value. patch_send_to must result in a user-turn appearing in the target chat. patch_spawn must create a new chat with a new chatId.

name: Daemon — notifications, voice event queue, broadcast sidecars

tasks.task:
The daemon handles all outbound notification delivery and maintains the broadcast sidecar mechanism that gives Speakers and Telegram threads context for user replies.

Verify and repair, testing each channel:

patch_notify routing — push channel: daemon forwards to server which fans out via FCM (firebase-admin). Delivery is suppressed if any surface sent surface.heartbeat within the last 30s — unless priority: urgent, which overrides. FCM errors logged to /data/undelivered.jsonl.

patch_notify routing — desktop channel: daemon forwards the notify event to any connected desktop notifier surface. Always fires when the notifier is connected regardless of other presence. OS toast on the notifier end.

patch_notify routing — telegram channel: daemon posts the message directly to the Telegram bot API (using grammy) without routing through the Telegram thread's agent. No thread record in the session JSONL. Errors logged to /data/undelivered.jsonl.

patch_notify routing — speakers channel: daemon resolves the target device in order: (1) explicit deviceId in the call, (2) most-recently-active device, (3) all devices at low volume, (4) push fallback if all devices offline. Sends a ring frame with conversational: false over the device's control WSS. On accept, streams Kokoro TTS. Muted devices are always skipped. Voice device specifics are covered in group F2 — for this group, test that the routing resolution logic and fallback chain work correctly with mock devices.

patch_call: rings all registered surfaces simultaneously. First accept wins, others receive a cancel. After 30s with no accept (or all decline), falls back to push notification carrying the reason text. Test with both phone and desktop surfaces.

Broadcast sidecar: for each of Speakers and Telegram threads, daemon maintains an append-only broadcast log at ~/.patch/threads/{speakers,telegram}/broadcasts.jsonl. Each entry is {ts, sourceChatName, message}. Written by daemon immediately when delivering a notify on that channel. When a real user reply arrives in the Speakers or Telegram thread, daemon reads the sidecar and prepends a <system-reminder> block to the SDK query() prompt containing recent broadcasts (relative timestamps, newest last). Format: 'Recent broadcasts delivered on this thread (newest last): - 5 min ago: "message" (from chat: name)'. Sidecar is flushed (truncated to empty) after the agent commits a response to the user's reply. If the agent invocation fails, sidecar is NOT flushed — broadcasts persist for next attempt. Mid-turn broadcast arrivals land in the sidecar but are deferred to the next turn. Sidecar capped at 10k chars; truncate oldest first if exceeded.

tasks.task:
The three special threads (Manager, Telegram, Speakers) are persistent single chats with dedicated ingress channels. They differ from regular chats only in their ingress plumbing and role — not in their tool surface.

Verify and repair:

Thread creation: on first daemon start, create ~/.patch/threads/{manager,telegram,speakers}/ folders and an empty CLAUDE.md in each. Do not write content into the CLAUDE.md and never overwrite existing content. Register each thread as a regular chat with a stable chatId stored in daemon state (survives restart). Never create more than one instance of each thread.

Manager thread: ingress via web and mobile text composer plus voice queue (covered in voice groups). Manager sits at the top of the sidebar on both web and mobile (first dedicated slot, above pinned chats). The text composer is enabled. Manager's cross-chat tools (patch_spawn, patch_send_to, patch_call, patch_job_create etc.) must be reachable from within the Manager session.

Telegram thread: ingress via Telegram bot (messages routed from server's /telegram/webhook endpoint). Messages from TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USER_ID only — others silently dropped at the server before reaching the thread. When the Telegram agent produces a direct reply (the turn following an inbound Telegram message), that reply is automatically sent to the user's Telegram via the bot API — no explicit patch_notify call needed. This reply routing is enforced by the daemon, not by the agent. Composer is disabled on web and mobile (read-only mirror). Telegram + Speakers live in the Channels section of the sidebar (collapsed by default).

Speakers thread: ingress is audio from physical voice devices (covered in voice device groups — F1/F2). Each inbound audio turn is tagged [voice • device] with deviceId. Composer is disabled. When the Speakers agent produces a direct reply, it auto-routes as TTS to the originating device (deviceId from the inbound turn). The Speakers thread agent must not delegate questions ('how are my jobs going?') through Manager — it calls patch_list_chats and patch_peek itself.

Broadcast context for both Speakers and Telegram: when the user sends a reply in either thread, the daemon injects recent broadcasts as a <system-reminder> block (tested in C3 — verify integration here).

Thread folder structure: each thread folder is a sub-folder under the daemon's startup cwd (.patch/threads/<name>/) so Claude Code inherits the parent CLAUDE.md and skills via directory walking. Verify this inheritance works for a real session by checking that skills in the parent directory are available inside a thread session.

Test: send a Telegram message as the allowed user → it appears in the Telegram thread; send from another user ID → silently dropped; Telegram agent reply → reaches Telegram bot automatically; Speakers turn from deviceId 'kitchen' → reply auto-routes back to kitchen device; Manager at top of sidebar; Channels section is collapsed by default; special thread folders and CLAUDE.md created on first start.

name: Triggers — cron, webhook, calendar, Todoist, job execution

tasks.task:
Jobs are the cross-session automation layer. A job is a trigger + optional filter + one action stored in /data/jobs/<id>.json. The server fires all triggers; the daemon executes all actions. The agent that created the job is not involved at fire time.

Verify and repair every trigger type, the filter mechanism, and both action types:

Cron trigger: stored as a 5-field UTC cron expression. Server's in-process cron scheduler (node-cron) fires at the correct UTC time. Payload to filter/action: {firedAt: ISO timestamp}. TZ env is applied only when displaying or parsing natural-language input in the UI/CLI — never stored as non-UTC.

Webhook trigger: server validates HMAC signature per configured scheme (none/hmac-sha256/github/stripe). On pass, extracts payload and applies filter. Every inbound webhook hit logged to /data/webhooks/<jobId>.jsonl including failures.

Google Calendar trigger: server subscribes to Calendar push notifications via googleapis. On event: the matched event object is the payload. GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET must be configured.

Todoist trigger: server subscribes to Todoist webhook using TODOIST_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Task objects matching the filter are the payload.

JSONata filter: applied to the trigger payload. Truthy → action fires. Falsy → logged as filter-rejected (no run). Error → logged as filter-error. Evaluation is synchronous and takes microseconds (no LLM). Uses the jsonata library.

Spawn action: creates a fresh chat in the specified folder. The new chat defaults to archived state (not the active inbox — background automation). If the action carries a skill, the chat receives /<skill-name>\n<trigger-payload-as-JSON> as its first user turn. If the action carries a prompt, mustache-substitute {{payload.field}} values.

Message action: delivers into an existing chat via chatId. Same skill/prompt logic as spawn. patch_send_to is what this uses under the hood — distinct from spawn but same substitution mechanics.

All four action combinations must work: spawn+skill, spawn+prompt, message+skill, message+prompt.

Every job fire (whether success, filter-rejected, filter-error, or dispatch-error) is appended to /data/runs/<jobId>.jsonl with {ts, jobId, status, trigger, payloadDigest, action?}. Run logs are non-fsync'd appends.

CLI CRUD (patch jobs list/get/create/update/delete/enable/disable/runs/hooks) and MCP tool CRUD (patch_job_create/list/update/delete/enable/disable/runs/webhooks) must both work and operate on the same /data/jobs/*.json source.

Offline buffering: if daemon is offline when an action should fire, action is stored in /data/pending/ and flushed on reconnect (already tested in D3 — verify integration here with a real job).

Test: create a cron job with a 1-minute expression → verify it fires and spawns a chat; create a webhook job → POST to the URL → verify dispatch; create a job with a JSONata filter → post a matching payload → fires; post a non-matching payload → filter-rejected in runs log; verify all four action combinations each produce the correct first user turn.

notes: Cron, webhook, JSONata filter, all four action combinations, run/webhook logging, CLI/MCP store parity, and offline buffering are testable on the dev mock stack. Google Calendar and Todoist triggers are ENV-GATED (require GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID/SECRET and TODOIST_WEBHOOK_SECRET + live push subscriptions) and are NOT executable on the local mock stack — they are intentionally omitted from the executable set rather than authored as guaranteed-blocker tests; cover them in a deployment/integration pass (H1) where real credentials exist.

tasks.task:
The system must degrade gracefully on any disconnect without losing conversation state or committed events. Disconnects are expected; silent data loss is not acceptable.

Verify and repair every scenario against a running server+daemon stack by intentionally killing connections:

Surface → server disconnect: surface detects WS close, shows 'reconnecting...' banner in UI. Retries with exponential backoff (1s → 2s → 5s → 10s, max 30s). On reconnect: sends hello frame then chat.replay {chatId, fromSeq} for every open chat. Server relays replay request to daemon. Daemon streams missed events from its persisted history. User messages typed while disconnected are queued in-memory on the surface; emitted in order on reconnect. If the surface process is killed before reconnect, the queued messages are lost — the UI must show a 'not sent' indicator for any message in this state.

Daemon → server disconnect (one process dies while the other stays up): daemon detects WS close, marks itself as reconnecting. In-flight SDK query() runs continue locally. Outbound events (chat messages, tool calls) buffer in daemon memory, bounded at 10k events per chat — drop oldest with a log warning if exceeded. On reconnect: daemon sends all buffered events in order. Server marks daemon as online again, surfaces receive daemon.online and their chats re-sync.

Daemon process death: all in-flight SDK queries die (SDK is in-process — no orphan subprocesses). Claude Code's native session history on disk is unaffected (already persisted by the SDK). On restart: daemon scans ~/.patch/chats/*/meta.json, marks all chats idle. Next user message for any chat triggers fresh query() with resume: meta.claudeSessionId. SDK reconstructs context from the JSONL. If claudeSessionId is missing/invalid, chat is marked errored. Server receives daemon.offline during the gap, then daemon.online on reconnect.

Voice WSS drop mid-session: audio session ends. Surface shows 'voice disconnected' and falls back to text input. Voice device LED goes to disconnected state. On reconnect, the next voice session starts fresh — audio sessions are not replayed. If a voice user-turn was transcribed but not yet delivered to its chat when WSS dropped: daemon retries delivery on reconnect. If retry fails within 10s, surface is told 'delivery failed, try again'.

Sequence replay correctness: events carry per-chat monotonic seq. A surface that reconnects and replays from seq N must receive exactly the events it missed without gaps or duplicates.

chat.input localId dedup: if a surface sends the same chat.input event twice (e.g. retry on flaky connection), the second one must be silently dropped — the daemon tracks (chatId, localId) pairs. No duplicate user messages.

Test: simulate surface disconnect → reconnect → verify replay fills in missed messages; simulate daemon crash → restart → verify chat resumes and seq is correct; test localId dedup by sending the same chat.input twice; verify 10k buffer cap is enforced.

steps: Start a chat so ~/.patch/chats/<id>/meta.json records a claudeSessionId.

Confirm the server observes daemon.offline.

Observe events received during the gap.
Restore the daemon.
Observe events after reconnect.

name: Voice daemon pipeline — Whisper, Kokoro, AEC, barge-in

tasks.task:
The daemon hosts the complete voice pipeline used by all surfaces — phone, web, and standalone voice device. The same engine serves all of them. No third-party voice service is used for TTS; Whisper STT can be Groq-hosted or local.

Verify and repair, testing with an actual voice session from web or phone against the running daemon:

Audio WSS endpoint: daemon accepts voice surface connections authenticated with a per-session voiceToken (HMAC-signed, minted by daemon or fetched from server on device's behalf). The voiceToken is not a reusable credential — it is per-session. surfaceKind field identifies the connecting surface (phone, web, device).

Whisper STT (Groq path, default): daemon streams inbound PCM16 audio to Groq's Whisper large-v3-turbo REST endpoint. End-of-utterance is detected via Silero-VAD on the daemon side or Whisper's own EOS heuristics. On end-of-utterance, daemon emits the transcribed text as a user-turn message to currentChatId with [voice • <surface>] prefix prepended. The prefix is metadata — it is not a system prompt injection.

Whisper STT (local path, WHISPER_BACKEND=local): daemon spawns a faster-whisper Python sidecar (uv run → FastAPI, PCM in via WS, transcript out) using the model at WHISPER_MODEL_PATH. Same interface for the rest of the pipeline.

Kokoro TTS: a long-running Python sidecar (same shape as faster-whisper). Streams 24 kHz mono PCM16 frames. Daemon sends agent response text to Kokoro per-sentence as Claude streams tokens. Kokoro returns audio frames that daemon streams back over the audio WSS. Streaming is true end-to-end: Kokoro starts speaking on the first sentence boundary while Claude Code is still generating later tokens. KOKORO_MODEL_PATH from env.

Focus-follow: a module-level currentChatId is maintained per voice session. When the surface emits chat.focus_change {chatId}, daemon updates currentChatId so the next utterance lands in the new chat. The audio WSS stays open across focus changes.

Barge-in: Silero-VAD (via onnxruntime-node, model shipped as ONNX) runs continuously on the AEC-cleaned inbound mic stream even while Kokoro is streaming TTS to the surface. When VAD fires (user speaking), daemon stops the Kokoro stream immediately, drops all in-flight TTS audio, and routes the new utterance to Whisper. This prevents the user from being stuck listening to a long response.

Daemon-side AEC: incoming raw mic audio has a delayed copy of the most-recently-transmitted TTS audio subtracted using a pure-TypeScript NLMS canceller. This cleans the mic signal before feeding it to Silero-VAD and Whisper, preventing the device or speaker playback from tripping the VAD. The AEC is applied to all non-phone/non-web voice sessions (phone and web have hardware/OS AEC). For voice devices, the daemon AEC is the only AEC — the HA Voice PE has no hardware AEC.

Permission prompts during voice: if Claude enters awaiting-permission mid-voice-session, daemon emits chat.permission_request over the audio WSS. Surface shows a banner with Approve/Deny. User can tap or speak 'yes'/'no'. Spoken response goes through the same Whisper path; daemon parses and emits chat.permission_response.

Python sidecar lifecycle: both Kokoro and faster-whisper sidecars are started on daemon boot and kept running permanently (not per-session). They must be restarted if they crash. KOKORO_MODEL_PATH and WHISPER_MODEL_PATH must be validated at startup — missing model files must abort with a clear error, not a silent failure.

Test: open a voice session from the web app → speak a sentence → verify it reaches the correct chat as a user turn with [voice • web] prefix; verify Kokoro TTS audio arrives back and plays; speak while agent is responding → verify barge-in stops TTS and transcribes the new utterance; navigate to a different chat mid-session → verify next utterance lands in the new chat.

tests.behaviour: A spoken utterance from a web/app voice session lands as a user-turn in the focused chat, tagged with a [voice • <surface>] metadata prefix (not an injected system prompt)
steps: Bring up the dev daemon+server in mock voice mode and obtain a per-session voice token for a known chat by exercising the surface-authenticated voice-token path (an authenticated surface credential is required to mint one).

Open the daemon's audio session over its audio WebSocket, complete the session-start handshake, then stream enough mic PCM to produce one completed utterance (the mock STT will yield a deterministic transcript).
Read that chat's history/turns and inspect the resulting user-turn message text exactly.
tests.expect: PASS = a new USER turn appears in the targeted chat whose content is the transcript prefixed with a [voice • <surface>] marker matching the connecting surface kind (e.g. web). The prefix must be ordinary turn TEXT/metadata prepended to the user message, NOT delivered as a separate system prompt or system-reminder. NOT qualifying: an HTTP 200 / token mint alone with no recorded turn; a turn that lacks the voice prefix; the prefix appearing on an assistant turn or as a system message; verifying against a chat other than the focused one.

tests.behaviour: Kokoro TTS audio for the agent reply streams back over the same audio session as binary PCM frames with start/end markers
steps: On an open mock voice session, drive one full utterance so the chat produces a reply.
Capture everything the daemon sends back on the audio channel after the transcript is finalised: both the JSON control envelopes and any binary audio frames.
Observe ordering relative to the reply being produced.
tests.expect: PASS = after the user turn the daemon emits a transcript-final control event, then one or more binary PCM audio frames accompanied by TTS-chunk control events, terminated by a TTS-end control event — i.e. synthesised audio is actually streamed back to the surface. NOT qualifying: only a transcript event with no audio frames; a single control event claiming completion with zero binary PCM emitted; the reply text appearing only in chat history but never synthesised onto the audio channel.

tests.behaviour: Barge-in: speaking while the agent's TTS is playing immediately halts the TTS stream and re-opens listening
steps: Drive a session into the speaking state (a reply whose TTS is actively streaming back).
While TTS frames are still being emitted, feed mic input that the VAD treats as the user starting to speak (the mock VAD can be driven to fire an utterance-start during speaking).
Watch the audio channel for what happens to the in-flight TTS, then complete the new utterance and check where it goes.
tests.expect: PASS = the moment user speech is detected during playback, the daemon emits a barge-in signal, stops sending further TTS PCM for the interrupted reply (drops in-flight audio), and a TTS-end marked as barged-in is sent; the subsequent utterance is transcribed and submitted as a fresh user turn. NOT qualifying: TTS continuing to stream to completion after the interruption; the new utterance being dropped or appended to the previous turn; the session erroring/closing instead of returning to listening.

tests.behaviour: Focus-follow: after the surface signals a focus change to a different chat, the audio session stays open and the next utterance lands in the NEW chat
steps: Open one voice session and confirm a first utterance lands in chat A.

Without closing the audio session, drive the focus-change mechanism the surface uses to re-point this session at chat B (discover how focus is delivered to the live session — do not assume an endpoint).
Produce a second utterance on the same still-open session and check which chat receives it.
tests.expect: PASS = the audio session remains open across the focus change (no reconnect), and the second utterance is recorded as a user turn in chat B while the first remains in chat A. NOT qualifying: the session closing/reopening to switch chats; the second utterance still landing in chat A; both utterances landing in the same chat; needing a brand-new token to change focus.

tests.behaviour: The audio WSS rejects any connection that does not present a valid session-start with a verifiable per-session voice token
steps: Open the daemon audio WebSocket and send a non-session-start frame first (e.g. binary PCM or some other control frame) — observe the daemon's response.
Open a fresh connection and send a session-start carrying a missing/garbage/tampered token — observe the response.
For contrast, confirm a session-start with a properly minted token for the matching identity IS accepted.
tests.expect: PASS = both the no-handshake case and the bad-token case are refused (the daemon returns an audio error and closes the socket) while the correctly-minted token is accepted and the session proceeds. The rejection must be on the token/handshake itself. NOT qualifying: the daemon accepting audio frames before a valid session-start; accepting a token whose signature/claims do not verify; only the malformed-JSON case being rejected while a forged-but-well-formed token slips through.

tests.behaviour: The voice token is single-use per session — a replayed token is rejected on a second session-start
steps: Mint one voice token and use it to successfully open an audio session.
Attempt to open a second audio session presenting the exact same token (same session id).
Observe whether the second attempt is admitted.
tests.expect: PASS = the first session opens; the second attempt with the same token is refused as a replay (audio error + socket close), proving the token is not a reusable credential. NOT qualifying: the second session opening successfully; the rejection being attributable to something other than reuse (e.g. an unrelated identity mismatch); the token being accepted again after the first session merely closed.

tests.behaviour: The voice-token mint endpoint refuses an unauthenticated caller
steps: Probe the server's voice-session-token mint path with NO bearer credential and observe the status.
Probe it with a malformed/invalid surface credential and observe the status.
Confirm the same request with the dev harness's valid surface credential succeeds and returns a token bound to the requested chat/role/surface.
tests.expect: PASS = missing and invalid credentials both yield a 401-class rejection with no token issued, while a valid surface credential yields a token. NOT qualifying: a token being minted without any credential; the endpoint 500ing instead of cleanly rejecting; a token being returned that is not bound to the authenticated surface identity.

tests.behaviour: A device-kind voice session must carry its originating deviceId; the coupling is enforced at session-start
steps: Open an audio session declaring surfaceKind device but WITHOUT a deviceId and observe the result.
Open an audio session declaring a non-device surfaceKind (e.g. web) but supplying a deviceId and observe the result.
Confirm a device session that DOES carry a deviceId is accepted.
tests.expect: PASS = the device-without-deviceId and non-device-with-deviceId cases are both rejected at session-start (invalid-frame style error + close), and the correctly-coupled device session is accepted. This guarantees a device turn can be tagged/routed back to its room. NOT qualifying: either malformed coupling being silently accepted; the deviceId being ignored rather than validated.

tests.behaviour: Concurrent voice sessions are capped; the over-limit session is refused with a concurrency error rather than degrading silently
steps: Determine the daemon's configured concurrent-session cap for the running backend (read it from code/config rather than assuming a number).
Open that many simultaneous valid audio sessions and keep them open.
Open one more valid session and observe how the daemon responds.
tests.expect: PASS = sessions up to the cap open normally; the session beyond the cap is refused with an explicit concurrency-cap audio error and closed, leaving the existing sessions intact. NOT qualifying: the extra session silently displacing an existing one; the daemon crashing or hanging; the cap not being enforced at all (Nth+1 admitted).

tests.behaviour: With a REAL voice backend selected but its required model/credential absent, the daemon fails loudly — no silent fallback to mock or skipping
steps: Configure the daemon to use a real STT or TTS backend (the non-mock path) while deliberately omitting the required model path / API credential for it.
Attempt to boot the voice pipeline (or perform the first synthesis/transcription that needs it).
Observe whether it aborts with a clear message naming the missing model/credential, or whether it proceeds anyway.
tests.expect: PASS = the daemon refuses with an explicit error that names the missing model file or credential (e.g. the Kokoro model path or the STT API key) — consistent with the spec's NO-FALLBACK rule. NOT qualifying: silently falling back to the mock backend; booting fine and only erroring with an opaque/unrelated message; quietly disabling voice while reporting healthy.

tests.behaviour: POST /api/voice/token mints a token for a chatId that does not exist or is not owned by the account
steps: Authenticate with a valid surface JWT (from .dev-data/.web-credential.json)
POST /api/voice/token with body {chatId:'DOES_NOT_EXIST_AT_ALL_XYZ', role:'voice-call', surfaceKind:'web'}
tests.expect: PASS = the mint endpoint validates chat existence/ownership and rejects an unknown chatId with a 4xx and a specific error (e.g. chat_not_found) BEFORE issuing a token. Currently it returns 200 with a usable token+sessionId+audioUrl which does NOT qualify. Returning 200 for any garbage chatId is a fail.

tests.behaviour: A voice token is not bound to the chatId it was minted for; a session_start can declare a different chatId
steps: Mint a voice token via POST /api/voice/token for chatId A
Open ws://127.0.0.1:3013/audio/<sessionId> and send audio.session_start with the SAME token but chatId set to a DIFFERENT value B (matching accountId/surfaceId/sessionId)
Observe whether the daemon accepts the session
tests.expect: PASS = the daemon rejects the session_start with audio.error (auth_failed or invalid_frame) because the declared chatId does not match the chatId the token was minted for. Currently the session is accepted silently (no error event, no close) because the token claims omit chatId, which does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: Streaming speech to a session bound to a non-existent chat fails late with a generic sdk_error after full STT instead of failing fast
steps: Mint a token for a non-existent chatId and open the audio WSS, sending session_start
Stream real PCM speech (e.g. models/kokoro/samples/af_heart_0.wav at 16k in 480-sample frames) followed by silence
Observe the sequence of audio.* events
tests.expect: PASS = the session is rejected at session_start time (or before STT runs) with a SPECIFIC error code identifying the missing chat (e.g. session_not_found). Currently the daemon runs Whisper to completion, emits audio.transcript_final, and only THEN emits the generic audio.error:sdk_error (ChatNotFoundError); running STT first and using the catch-all sdk_error code does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: Audio WSS closes rejected connections with WS close code 1005 (no status) instead of a meaningful close code
steps: Open ws://127.0.0.1:3013/audio/<sessionId> and trigger any rejection (e.g. binary frame before session_start, or a forged token in session_start)
Capture the WebSocket close event's code and reason on the client
tests.expect: PASS = the audio WSS closes rejected connections with an explicit close code + reason (matching the /ws hub convention of 4400 malformed-frame / 4401 auth). Currently every rejectConn path calls bare ws.close() so the client observes code 1005 with empty reason; code 1005/empty reason does NOT qualify. The preceding audio.error event still carries the code, but the close frame itself must be explicit.

tests.behaviour: GET /api/daemon/healthz is reachable without authentication while sibling authed endpoints require a Bearer token
steps: GET http://127.0.0.1:3010/api/daemon/healthz with NO Authorization header
For comparison, GET /api/jobs and /api/auth/me with no auth
tests.expect: PASS = /api/daemon/healthz either requires auth (401 without a Bearer, consistent with the other /api/daemon/* and /api/jobs endpoints) OR the spec explicitly documents it as a public probe. Currently it returns 200 {ok:true} unauthenticated while /api/jobs and /api/auth/me return 401; an undocumented unauthenticated daemon-status leak does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: POST /api/chats returns a chatId in its 400 folder_not_found error for a chat that was never created
steps: Authenticate with a valid surface JWT
POST /api/chats with body {folder:'/nonexistent/path/xyz123'}
Inspect the 400 response body, then GET /api/chats to confirm the returned chatId was not persisted
tests.expect: PASS = the 400 folder_not_found error body does NOT include a chatId field (no ID is surfaced for a chat that was never created). Currently the 400 response carries a chatId (e.g. 01KV9Z48...) that is absent from the subsequent /api/chats list; returning a misleading chatId on a failed creation does NOT qualify.

name: Voice device firmware (HA Voice Preview Edition)

tasks.task:
The HA Voice Preview Edition (ESP32-S3) is re-flashed with patch's custom firmware. The device is a surface — it captures and plays audio. All intelligence (STT, TTS, Claude) runs on the daemon. This firmware is not optional — the Speakers thread and speakers notify channel depend on it.

Verify and repair the firmware in packages/voice-firmware, built with ESP-IDF + idf.py (not Arduino, not ESPHome, not PlatformIO):

microWakeWord: runs on-device using TFLite Micro models (same models HA Assist uses). Detects the configured wake word with acceptable false-positive rate. Triggers session start.

Control WSS (persistent): device maintains a persistent WebSocket connection to the paired daemon. Sends hello frame {type: 'hello', deviceId, fwVersion, muted} on connect. Connection uses the device's auth token obtained during QR-pairing. Reconnects with exponential backoff on Wi-Fi drop or WS close.

Wake-word flow: on wake-word detection, device sends {type: 'wake_detected'} on the control WSS. Daemon responds with {type: 'session_start', sessionId, voiceToken}. Device opens the audio WSS authenticated with voiceToken. Streams PCM16 mono 16kHz mic audio to daemon. Plays PCM16 24kHz TTS audio received from daemon. Session ends when device sends {type: 'session_end', reason} or daemon closes the audio WSS.

Push-to-talk: holding the button also opens an audio session (same flow, button-released = session_end reason 'user-button').

LED ring: shows exactly these 9 states via WS2812: idle (off or dim ambient), wake-detected (single pulse), listening (steady cyan), agent-speaking (pulsing white), ringing (yellow rotation), muted (solid red), disconnected (slow red pulse), pairing-in-progress (blue rotation), pairing-failed (magenta double pulse).

Mute switch: hardware I2S mic mute detected → firmware stops microWakeWord processing, drops any in-flight audio session, sends {type: 'mute_changed', muted: true} on control WSS, LED solid red. On unmute: resumes microWakeWord, sends mute_changed: false.

Patch-initiated ring: daemon sends {type: 'ring', chatId, message?, conversational} on control WSS. Device plays a chime, LED goes yellow rotation. Button press → sends ring_accepted → daemon sends session_start → audio WSS opens → daemon streams Kokoro TTS of the queued message. If conversational: true, audio WSS stays open for bidirectional exchange. If 30s passes without acceptance → device sends ring_dismissed. If device is muted → daemon must not send ring frame (this is daemon-side logic, but firmware must correctly report mute state).

OTA updates: implemented via esp_https_ota pulling signed images from the patch server. Device polls for updates on boot.

QR-code device pairing: device displays QR with pairing nonce in firmware's pairing mode (button held at boot or new device). Paired via the standard surface-linking flow (10-auth.md). Device stores deviceId and auth credentials in NVS.

Audio path uses esp_codec_dev for INMP441 mic and MAX98357A speaker. Audio WSS and control WSS use esp_websocket_client.

Test: flash device and verify: wake word triggers session; LED transitions correctly through all states; mute switch engages and disengages correctly; ring from daemon causes chime + yellow LED + audio session on accept; ring times out at 30s; audio round-trip latency is within expected bounds (~600ms–1s with Groq STT path).

tests.behaviour: The pure-C firmware state machines build and pass their host-side unit harness clean under ASan/UBSan
steps: Locate the off-device host-test harness for the voice firmware (the C state-machine test suite that does NOT need the ESP-IDF toolchain or a flashed board) and build every test executable from a clean tree before running them.
Run the full suite and read the per-suite results, not just the exit code.
Confirm the harness is actually compiled with the address + undefined-behaviour sanitisers enabled (a sanitiser hit must fail the run, not be ignored).
tests.expect: PASS = the suite builds from clean and every test case passes (the suites cover the control-frame codec, the device-state FSM, the ring FSM, the LED pattern table, the boot check, the mic-pump invariants and the button classifier). NOT qualifying: a 'cmake/build succeeded' with the tests never run; a green ctest line that ran zero cases because the executables were not built first; suppressing or not enabling the sanitisers. Any sanitiser report (ASan/UBSan) is a FAIL.
tests.result_note: PASS. host_test built clean from a fresh tree (rm -rf build; cmake -S . -B build; cmake --build build) with -fsanitize=address,undefined via /opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/clang (ASan runtime libclang_rt.asan_osx_dynamic.dylib linked into the test binaries, 95 asan symbols in test_button). ctest: 7/7 PASS (test_control_frames, test_device_state, test_ring_fsm, test_led_table, test_boot_check, test_mic_pump_state, test_button), no sanitiser reports.

tests.behaviour: Control-frame codec encodes every device->daemon frame and decodes every daemon->device frame exactly per the wire spec, rejecting malformed and ignoring unknown frames
steps: Exercise the firmware's control-frame encode path for each outbound frame the device sends (hello with deviceId/fwVersion/muted, wake_detected, session_end with each reason, ring_accepted, ring_dismissed, mute_changed) and confirm the produced JSON matches the spec's frame shapes in spec/16-voice-device.md, including that session_end reason strings are exactly vad-timeout | user-button | agent-finished.

Exercise the decode path for each inbound frame (session_start, ring, led, error) and confirm required fields are extracted (e.g. session_start.sessionId, ring.chatId + conversational + optional message).
Feed malformed JSON and a frame with an unrecognised type and observe the codec's handling.
tests.expect: PASS = each outbound frame round-trips to the spec-exact JSON (correct reason enums), each inbound frame decodes its required fields, malformed input returns an explicit parse/missing error (never a silently coerced default), and an unknown frame type is reported as unknown-frame (ignore-with-log) rather than crashing. NOT qualifying: a decoder that fills missing required fields with defaults; treating an unknown frame as a known one; accepting an out-of-set session_end reason.
