name: Voice device routing — presence, outbound ring, multi-device

tasks.task:
The daemon manages voice device presence and controls outbound routing when something wants to speak to a physical device. This group covers daemon-side logic (F1 covers device firmware).

Verify and repair:

Device registration: when a device's control WSS connects and sends a hello frame with deviceId, daemon registers the device as online with {deviceId, name, online: true, muted: false, lastUsedAt}. When the control WSS drops, daemon marks device offline. patch_list_devices() returns this list accurately.

Mute state tracking: when device sends {type: 'mute_changed', muted: bool}, daemon updates the device's muted flag. A muted device must not be selected as a ring target.

patch_notify(channel: 'speakers') resolution: daemon resolves which device to ring in this order: (1) explicit deviceId in the call → ring that device; (2) most-recently-active online+unmuted device; (3) all online+unmuted devices at low volume (general announcement); (4) all devices offline or muted → fall through to push notification with the text content. In step (4), the message is not silently dropped — it becomes a push notification.

Ring flow (notifications, conversational: false): daemon sends {type: 'ring', chatId, message, conversational: false} to the selected device(s). On ring_accepted → daemon sends session_start with voiceToken → device opens audio WSS → daemon synthesises Kokoro TTS of the message and streams it → session ends. No listening period after TTS completes.

Ring flow (calls, conversational: true): same start, but after TTS completes, audio WSS stays open. Daemon listens for user speech, transcribes via Whisper, routes to voice-device chat, synthesises response, continues until session_end. This is the wake-word conversation model.

Voice-device chat routing: each inbound user-turn from a device carries deviceId. Daemon prepends [voice • device] metadata plus the deviceId to the user-turn text before delivering to the Speakers thread. The Speakers thread agent receives context about which device the utterance came from.

AEC for device sessions: since the HA Voice PE has no hardware AEC, daemon applies its TypeScript NLMS AEC to all device audio sessions. The AEC subtracts the TTS audio the daemon just sent to the device from the incoming mic audio. Barge-in (covered in E1) runs on the AEC-cleaned signal.

Concurrency: a phone-active call takes priority over idle devices. If a device session is already active when another voice event arrives, the new event is queued. Priority order: phone-active-call > device-active-session > idle devices > push notification. This logic must be tested with concurrent voice sessions.

Voice token delivery: the device never calls the server's voice-token endpoint directly — daemon mints or fetches the token and delivers it in the session_start control frame. Device uses it only for the audio WSS.

Test: register two devices; patch_notify with explicit deviceId → only that device rings; patch_notify without deviceId → most-recently-active device rings; mute that device → falls to next candidate; all devices offline → push notification fires; concurrent phone call + device ring → phone takes priority.

tests.behaviour: A device's control-WSS hello registers it as online; control-WSS drop marks it offline, and patch_list_devices reflects both transitions accurately
steps: Bring up the live daemon and open a device control connection that speaks the firmware's exact control-frame contract (a recording listener or the provided mock device), sending the initial hello identifying a deviceId, a name, and muted=false.
Read the daemon's device roster (via patch_list_devices through the MCP child, cross-checked against the daemon's internal device-list route).
Now cleanly drop that control connection and re-read the roster.
tests.expect: PASS = after hello the device appears with {deviceId, name, online:true, muted:false, lastUsedAt}; after the connection drops the SAME device is reported online:false. NOT qualifying: a device that never appears after hello, a device that stays online:true after the socket is gone, or a roster that omits the required fields (deviceId/name/online/muted/lastUsedAt).

tests.behaviour: A mute_changed frame updates the device's muted flag, and a muted device is never selected as a ring target
steps: Register an online, unmuted device over the control link and confirm it is the chosen target for a speakers notify with no explicit deviceId.
Have that device send mute_changed{muted:true} over the control link; confirm the roster now shows muted:true for it.
Fire a speakers notify again (no explicit deviceId) and observe which device, if any, receives the ring frame.
tests.expect: PASS = after mute_changed the device's muted flag flips true in the roster AND it is no longer sent a ring frame — the routing skips it (to the next candidate, or push fallback if none). NOT qualifying: the muted flag not updating, or a ring frame still being delivered to the muted device. A 200 from the notify call alone is NOT proof — you must observe that no ring frame reached the muted device's control socket.

tests.behaviour: speakers resolution step 1: an explicit deviceId in the notify call rings exactly that device and no other
steps: Register two online, unmuted devices over their control links, each with a distinct deviceId.
Fire a speakers-channel notify carrying an explicit deviceId naming one of them.
Inspect which device sockets received a ring frame.
tests.expect: PASS = only the explicitly-named device receives a ring frame (conversational:false for a notify); the other device receives nothing. NOT qualifying: both devices ringing, the wrong device ringing, or a returned-200 with no observed ring frame on the named device's socket.

tests.behaviour: speakers resolution step 2: with no explicit deviceId the most-recently-active online+unmuted device is chosen
steps: Register two online, unmuted devices; arrange that one of them had a more recent session/activity than the other (e.g. drive a session on one so its lastUsedAt is newer).
Fire a speakers notify with NO explicit deviceId.
Inspect which device socket received the ring frame.
tests.expect: PASS = the device with the more recent activity (newer lastUsedAt, within the recency window) is the one rung; the stale device is not. NOT qualifying: the older device being chosen, both being rung, or selection that ignores lastUsedAt ordering.

tests.behaviour: speakers cascade step 4: when every device is offline or muted, the message is NOT dropped — it becomes a push notification carrying the text
steps: Put the stack in a state where there is no reachable speaker device (all registered devices offline or muted, or none registered).
Fire a speakers-channel notify with a distinctive message body.
Observe the notification routing side effect — specifically whether a push notification carrying that text was produced.
tests.expect: PASS = the speakers notify falls through to a push notification whose payload carries the original message text (voicemail behaviour). NOT qualifying: the message being silently dropped, an error returned with no push fallback, or a ring frame being sent to a muted/offline device anyway.

tests.behaviour: Notification ring flow (conversational:false): on ring_accepted the daemon sends session_start with a voiceToken and the session does not stay open to listen after TTS
steps: Register an online unmuted device on a control listener that records every frame the daemon sends it.
Fire a speakers notify (one-way announcement) targeting that device; confirm the device receives a ring frame with conversational:false.
Have the recording device reply ring_accepted and observe the daemon's follow-up control frame.
After the (silent) TTS streaming would complete, observe whether the session remains open for a listening turn.
tests.expect: PASS = the ring frame carries conversational:false; ring_accepted triggers a session_start frame that includes a voiceToken; after the announcement the session ends with no post-TTS listening window. NOT qualifying: a session_start with no voiceToken, conversational:true on a plain notify, or the session staying open to listen after a one-way announcement. Do not play any audio to verify — inspect the control frames and any PCM frames programmatically.

tests.behaviour: Conversational ring flow (conversational:true): after TTS the audio session stays open for the user's spoken reply (wake-word conversation model)
steps: Trigger a conversational voice ring to a recording device (e.g. via the patch_call / agent-initiated voice path that sets conversational:true), distinct from the one-way notify path.
Have the device accept; observe the session_start and that the daemon keeps the audio WSS open after the initial TTS rather than ending the session.
Confirm the contrast with the notification flow from F2-6 (which closes after speaking).
tests.expect: PASS = the conversational ring keeps the audio session open after the initial spoken message so a user reply can be transcribed and routed, ending only on session_end/VAD-timeout. NOT qualifying: a conversational ring that closes immediately like a one-way announcement, or no observable difference between the conversational and notification flows.

tests.behaviour: Each inbound voice-device turn is tagged with [voice • device] plus the originating deviceId before delivery to the Speakers thread
steps: Drive an inbound voice turn from a device with a known deviceId (an utterance routed through the device's audio/control path to the voice-device chat).
Read the resulting user-turn as it lands in the Speakers thread (history/peek).
tests.expect: PASS = the user-turn delivered to the Speakers thread carries the [voice • device] metadata AND the originating deviceId, so the agent knows the utterance came from voice and from which device. NOT qualifying: a bare user-turn with no voice tag, or a tag that omits the deviceId.

tests.behaviour: Daemon-side AEC is applied to device audio sessions: the incoming mic stream has the just-sent TTS subtracted before VAD/STT
steps: Locate how the daemon wires AEC into a device audio session (it has no hardware AEC, so the daemon's NLMS AEC must process device-session inbound audio).
Exercise a device audio session where known TTS PCM was streamed out and a mic frame containing an echo of that TTS is fed back in, and inspect the signal that reaches VAD/STT.
Confirm the cleaned signal has the reference TTS attenuated relative to the raw mic input (inspect PCM frames numerically — never play audio).
tests.expect: PASS = device audio sessions route inbound mic audio through the daemon's AEC, measurably attenuating the echoed TTS reference before the signal reaches VAD/STT (so the device does not barge in on its own playback). NOT qualifying: device sessions that bypass AEC entirely, or AEC that is defined but never applied on the device-session path. Verify by inspecting PCM frame energy, not by listening.

tests.behaviour: Concurrency priority: a second voice event while a device session is active is QUEUED, not run in parallel; a second event for the already-active device is rejected
steps: Open and keep an active voice session on one device.
While it is active, deliver a new voice ring/wake event targeting a DIFFERENT idle device and observe whether it opens immediately or is held.
Separately, deliver a second event for the SAME already-active device and observe the outcome.
End the active session and observe whether a queued event is then released.
tests.expect: PASS = while a device session is active a new event for another device is queued (device-session-active) rather than opening a second parallel session, a second event for the already-active device is rejected (no self-queue), and ending the active session drains/releases the queued event. NOT qualifying: two device sessions opening concurrently, the queued event never being released, or the same-device event being queued instead of rejected.

tests.behaviour: Concurrency priority: an active phone Manager call outranks idle devices — a device voice event that lands during a phone-active call is held behind it
steps: Put the daemon in a state where a phone Manager voice call is active.
Deliver a device ring/wake voice event while the phone call is active and observe whether the device opens a session or is held.
End the phone call and observe whether the held device event is then released.
tests.expect: PASS = a device voice event arriving during an active phone call is queued behind it (phone-active-call outranks idle devices) and does not open a competing device session; when the phone call ends the queued device event is released. NOT qualifying: the device session opening in parallel with the active phone call, or the queued device event never being released after the call ends.

tests.behaviour: Voice token for a device session is daemon-supplied in session_start; the device never calls the server's voice-token mint endpoint, and its audio session identifies as surfaceKind 'device'
steps: Drive a device wake (or accepted-ring) session against a recording control+audio listener that captures both the session_start control frame and the audio session-start envelope.
Inspect where the voiceToken in the device's audio session-start comes from — confirm it is the token the daemon pushed in session_start, and that surfaceKind for the device session is 'device'.
Watch for ANY direct HTTP request from the device to the server's voice-token mint endpoint during the session.
tests.expect: PASS = the daemon mints/fetches the per-session voice token and delivers it in the session_start control frame; the device presents exactly that token (with surfaceKind 'device') when opening the audio WSS, and makes NO direct call to the server's voice-token endpoint. NOT qualifying: the device minting/fetching its own token, an audio session opened without the daemon-supplied token, or the device identifying as a web/desktop/mobile surface kind instead of 'device'.

tests.behaviour: A wake_detected frame sent BEFORE hello must not be granted a voice session on the device control plane
steps: Open ws://127.0.0.1:3013/device/control with a valid registered device JWT (kitchen-device-1)
Without sending the hello frame first, send {type:'wake_detected'}
Observe frames received and query the daemon roster GET /internal/devices over the daemon UDS
tests.expect: PASS = the daemon does NOT send a session_start frame for an un-helloed device (the wake is rejected/ignored until hello establishes presence), and the device never appears online. FAIL (current observed behaviour) = the daemon mints a real voiceToken and sends {type:'session_start',sessionId,voiceToken,chatId:'thread_speakers',conversational:true} even though the roster still shows online:false for that device — a session granted to an unidentified, presence-less device.

tests.behaviour: A queued device voice event must not fire session_start after the queued device's control socket has disconnected
steps: Connect kitchen-device-1 and bedroom-device-1 to /device/control (hello each), then send wake_detected on kitchen (admitted) and wake_detected on bedroom (queued behind kitchen)
While bedroom is still queued, terminate bedroom's WebSocket
Send {type:'session_end',reason:'agent-finished'} on kitchen to drain the queue
Inspect /tmp/patch-dev-daemon.log for bedroom device-offline vs session_start ordering
tests.expect: PASS = on drain the daemon re-validates the device is still connected; bedroom (offline) is dropped from the queue, NO session_start is minted/sent for it, and no concurrency slot is held by the gone device. FAIL (current observed behaviour) = log shows 'device offline' for bedroom THEN 'session_start sent' for bedroom (token minted + written to a closed socket) and the arbiter marks the disconnected device active ('released: bedroom-device-1'), leaking a slot no session_end/close will free.

tests.behaviour: There must be a wired daemon path that delivers a conversational (call) ring to a physical voice device
steps: Connect kitchen-device-1 to /device/control (hello)
Trigger the agent-initiated voice-call escalation path that targets a physical device (e.g. patch_call, or patch_notify on the voice/call channel) via the daemon UDS
Observe the ring frame the connected device receives
tests.expect: PASS = the connected device receives a {type:'ring',...,conversational:true} frame and, on ring_accepted, a conversational session_start — i.e. a speaker can be CALLED, not just notified. FAIL (current observed behaviour) = the only ring-producing path (patch_notify channel=speakers) always emits conversational:false, and patch_call never invokes the speakers cascade, so no caller ever produces a conversational ring to a device — physical speakers can only be notified, never called.

tests.behaviour: Concurrent device voice-session capacity on the control plane must match the documented whisper concurrency cap (3 for local-whisper dev)
steps: Connect kitchen-device-1 and bedroom-device-1 to /device/control (hello each)
Send wake_detected on kitchen, then ~300ms later wake_detected on bedroom (kitchen session still open)
Observe whether bedroom receives a session_start or is silently queued
tests.expect: PASS = both devices can hold a session up to the configured cap (defaultCap=3 for WHISPER_BACKEND==='local'), so the second device gets its own session_start rather than being blocked. FAIL (current observed behaviour) = the arbiter queues ANY second device event whenever activeDevices.size>0, so bedroom gets NO session_start while kitchen is active — the device control plane is effectively capped at 1 concurrent session, contradicting the documented cap of 3 (two separate speakers can never be in a voice session simultaneously).

name: CLI — interactive TUI and all management subcommands

tasks.task:
The patch CLI (packages/cli) is the canonical primitive surface. It is the remote control for the daemon and the interactive TUI for chat sessions. It must be a standalone Node binary built via pkg.

Verify and repair, testing each subcommand and TUI behaviour:

Interactive TUI (patch with no args): shows a folder picker listing recent folders from the daemon box plus a path text input. User picks or types, optionally adds an initial prompt, and a new chat is opened. The TUI renders the wire event stream identically to Claude Code's native output — messages, tool calls, diffs, permission prompts appear as they would from 'claude' locally.

Status strip: single line at the top of the terminal showing folder, chatId prefix (first 8 chars), and connection state. Connection state icon: 🟢 connected, 🟠 reconnecting, 🔴 offline, 🟡 phone active. Hideable with --no-status.

patch --folder /path: non-interactive spawn. Folder path must exist on the daemon box — validate and error loudly if not. Tab-completion for --folder is daemon-mediated (CLI queries daemon for filesystem listing).

Device handoff: when a phone surface takes over a chat that was focused in the terminal, terminal dims to 🟡 phone active and suspends input. Any key reclaims — CLI emits surface.foregrounded, phone surface observes and cedes.

Ctrl+B: opens a compact chat browser overlay (fuzzy-search across chat names, Enter to switch, Esc to close). Lightweight, no persistent sidebar.

Management subcommands (all tested with and without --json):
- patch resume [id]: resumes most recent chat or the chat matching the id prefix
- patch list [--active]: lists all chats (--active filters to running/awaiting-permission)
- patch attach <id>: reattaches to a live chat's TUI
- patch send <id> "msg": fire-and-forget user turn, exit 0
- patch history <id> [--limit N]: prints history to stdout
- patch stop <id>: terminates a chat
- patch auth login: OAuth + QR-link to existing account
- patch doctor: checks server reachability, daemon online/offline status, pending webhook/cron count, errored chat count

Resource-grouped subcommands (all with --json):
- patch chats list/get/spawn/send-to/stop/archive
- patch jobs list/get/create/update/delete/enable/disable/runs/hooks
- patch hooks list/tail [--id <id>]
- patch threads list / send-to <name> <message>
- patch surfaces list / ping <id>
- patch logs (tail daemon log)

Flag pass-through: --resume <chatId>, --model <model>, --dangerously-skip-permissions are translated into daemon spawn/resume options. Unknown flags produce clear error messages, not silent drops.

Config: ~/.patch/config.json with serverUrl and defaultFlags array. Per-invocation flags override config defaults.

Remote mode: when invoked off-box, CLI uses the public WebSocket server (HTTP mode with --remote <host> flag or PATCH_SERVER_URL from config) rather than the loopback Unix socket. Auth via QR-paired device credential.

Test: spawn a chat from CLI → stream events in TUI → stop it; send a message to a chat and see the response; run patch doctor against running stack and see correct output; verify --json output is valid JSON for each resource command; verify tab-completion of --folder calls the daemon.

tests.behaviour: Non-interactive spawn into a valid daemon-box folder opens a new chat
steps: Against the running dev stack (daemon + server), discover how the CLI spawns a chat non-interactively into a named folder (read the CLI to find the spawn primitive and the --folder form).
Pick a folder that genuinely exists on the daemon box, spawn a chat there, and capture the returned chatId.
Independently confirm via the chat-listing primitive (machine-readable output) that a NEW chat now exists bound to that folder.
tests.expect: PASS only if a brand-new chatId appears in the chat roster bound to the exact folder requested, AND the roster count increased by one. A zero exit code or printed chatId WITHOUT the chat actually appearing in an independent listing does NOT qualify; reusing a pre-existing chat does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: Spawning into a non-existent folder fails loudly with no chat created (NO FALLBACK)
steps: Attempt to spawn a chat into a path that does not exist on the daemon box (e.g. a random /tmp/does-not-exist-<rand>).
Observe the exit code and the error text.
List chats afterwards to confirm nothing was created.
tests.expect: PASS only if the CLI exits non-zero AND emits an explicit error that the folder does not exist (validated by the daemon), AND no new chat for that path appears in the roster. Silently succeeding, exit 0, creating a chat in the wrong/default folder, or swallowing the error does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: send delivers a user-turn into an existing chat fire-and-forget (exit 0)
steps: Spawn or pick a target chat T.
Use the CLI's fire-and-forget send primitive to deliver a uniquely-tagged message string into T.
Read T's history via the CLI (or the daemon's history route) and look for that exact message as a user turn.
tests.expect: PASS only if the exact tagged message appears as a user-turn in chat T's history AND the send command exited 0. A 0 exit or a 'queued' acknowledgement WITHOUT the message actually landing in T's recorded history does NOT qualify; the message appearing in a different chat does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: history prints a chat's events to stdout and honours the limit cap
steps: On a chat that has accumulated several turns, request its history in machine-readable form.
Repeat with an explicit small limit and confirm the count is bounded.
Pass an invalid limit (zero or negative or non-integer) and observe the result.
tests.expect: PASS only if history prints the chat's recorded events as valid machine-readable output, the small-limit run returns no more than the requested number, AND an invalid limit is rejected with a clear non-zero error. Printing an unbounded dump that ignores the limit, or silently coercing an invalid limit, does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: stop terminates a running chat and returns its activity to idle
steps: Drive a chat into a running state (e.g. send it a turn) and confirm via the listing primitive that its activity is running.
While it is running, issue the CLI stop command for that chat.
Re-read the chat's activity.
tests.expect: PASS only if the chat is observed running BEFORE the stop, and the stop returns ok AND the chat's activity returns to idle (query aborted) with the daemon still healthy. Stopping a chat that was already idle, or a 200/ok with the chat still showing running afterwards, does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: list and list --active reflect chat roster and activity filtering
steps: List all chats in machine-readable form and note which are running/awaiting-permission vs idle.
List again with the active-only filter.
Compare the two result sets.
tests.expect: PASS only if the unfiltered list contains every known chat (including special threads) and the active-only list is exactly the subset whose activity is running or awaiting-permission. Returning the same set for both, or omitting genuinely-active chats from the active list, does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: Every resource subcommand emits valid JSON under --json
steps: Enumerate the resource-grouped read commands the CLI exposes (chats, jobs, hooks, threads, surfaces, logs) by reading the CLI.
Invoke each list/read form with the machine-readable flag against the live stack.
Parse each stdout as JSON.
tests.expect: PASS only if EVERY read command's machine-readable output parses as a single well-formed JSON value with no human-readable prose mixed into stdout. Any command that emits a table, a stray log line, or non-parseable text on stdout under --json does NOT qualify; an error must itself be emitted as JSON on stdout (not bare text).

tests.behaviour: jobs CRUD round-trips through the CLI against the shared job store
steps: Create a job via the CLI (discover whether it takes a job-definition file) and capture its id.
List jobs and confirm it appears; disable then enable it; update a field; then delete it.
List again after delete.
tests.expect: PASS only if create yields an id, the job is visible in list, enable/disable flip its enabled state, update persists the changed field, and after delete it is absent — all reflected in the same job store the server/daemon use. A create that returns an id but does not appear in a subsequent list, or a delete that leaves the job present, does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: threads send-to resolves a thread by name and delivers into the correct special thread
steps: Use the CLI to send a uniquely-tagged message to a special thread by its NAME (manager/telegram/speakers), not by chatId.
Confirm via history/listing that the message landed in that specific special thread.
Send to an unknown thread name and observe the result.
tests.expect: PASS only if the tagged message appears in the named special thread's history AND an unknown thread name is rejected with a clear error naming the valid choices. Landing the message in the wrong thread, or silently accepting an unknown name, does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: doctor reports server reachability, daemon online/offline, errored-chat count, and pending backlog
steps: Run the diagnostics command against the live stack with the daemon up; capture its report.
Inspect the reported fields: server reachability, daemon online state, errored-chat count, pending cron/webhook backlog.
Optionally stop the daemon and re-run to confirm the daemon state flips to offline (not a hardcoded healthy value).
tests.expect: PASS only if the report shows server reachable=true, daemon online=true (with daemon up), a numeric errored-chat count, and a pending-backlog value — each derived from a real probe. If the daemon is stopped, the daemon state must flip to offline. A report that always shows healthy regardless of actual state, or that omits any of the four required signals, does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: An unknown top-level command or unknown flag fails loudly rather than silently launching the TUI or dropping the flag
steps: Invoke the CLI with a bareword command that does not exist (e.g. florp).
Invoke a real subcommand with a flag the CLI does not define.
Observe exit codes and stderr in each case.
tests.expect: PASS only if the unknown command exits non-zero naming the unknown command (and does NOT silently fall through to launching the interactive picker), AND the unknown flag produces a clear error rather than being silently dropped. Hanging on an interactive TUI, exit 0, or a misleading error does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: Daemon-mediated --folder completion sources candidates from the daemon box, and refuses in remote/REST mode
steps: Find how the CLI produces --folder tab-completion candidates (it is daemon-mediated, not from the CLI's local cwd).
With the local daemon socket available, request completions for a partial path that exists on the daemon box and confirm the candidates come from the daemon's filesystem.
Force the CLI into remote/REST mode (no local daemon socket) and request completion again.
tests.expect: PASS only if completion candidates are demonstrably the daemon box's filesystem listing (not the CLI's local directory), AND in remote/REST mode completion fails loudly with an explanatory error rather than silently completing against the local box. Completing against the CLI's own cwd, or silently returning empty, does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: config.json serverUrl/defaultFlags are honoured and per-invocation flags override config defaults
steps: Point the CLI at a config home containing a config.json with a known serverUrl and a defaultFlags array.
Run a command that consults the server and confirm it targets the configured serverUrl.
Provide a per-invocation override (e.g. an explicit server URL flag, or the server-URL env override) and confirm it wins over the config value.
tests.expect: PASS only if the configured serverUrl is used when no override is present AND a per-invocation override clearly takes precedence over the config default. Ignoring config.json, or letting the config value win over an explicit per-invocation override, does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: Remote mode talks to the server over HTTP/WebSocket using the paired credential rather than the loopback socket
steps: Configure the CLI so the local daemon socket is NOT used (remote posture: a server URL set, no reachable daemon socket / no local key) while a paired surface credential is available.
Run a read command (e.g. list chats) and confirm it succeeds via the server's HTTP API.
Run the same command with no/invalid credential and observe the failure.
tests.expect: PASS only if, in remote posture, the command reaches the server over HTTP using the paired bearer credential and returns the chat roster, AND a missing/invalid credential yields a clear auth error pointing at re-pairing/login. Falling back to the loopback socket, or succeeding without any credential, does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: patch daemon status/list work and the daemon clean subcommand exists and runs
steps: Run the daemon status subcommand against the live daemon and confirm it reports reachable/online.
Run the daemon list subcommand and confirm it returns the active chats.
Run the daemon clean subcommand (the spec lists start/stop/status/list/clean) and observe whether it is implemented.
tests.expect: PASS only if status reports the live daemon as reachable, list returns the chat roster, AND a clean subcommand is present and runs (removing stale chat metadata) rather than erroring as an unknown command. A missing clean subcommand, or status that reports healthy without probing, does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: Pass-through flags (--resume / --model / --dangerously-skip-permissions) are translated into daemon spawn/resume options, and the status strip renders folder + chatId prefix + connection state
steps: From the CLI source, identify where --resume/--model/--dangerously-skip-permissions and the single-line status strip are handled, then verify the wiring against the live stack WITHOUT entering the blocking interactive TUI loop (the interactive TUI requires a TTY and will hang — do not drive it interactively).

Confirm a resume/spawn invocation carrying these flags reaches the daemon as the corresponding spawn/resume options (observe the daemon-side effect or the request the CLI issues), and that an unmappable unknown flag errors clearly.
Confirm the status strip is built from folder, the first-8-chars chatId prefix, and a connection-state indicator, and that the suppress-status flag removes it.
tests.expect: PASS only if the three named flags demonstrably translate into daemon spawn/resume options (not silently dropped), an unknown unmappable flag errors clearly, AND the status strip content is folder + 8-char chatId prefix + connection state with a working suppress-status flag. If any flag is silently ignored, or the status strip omits one of the three elements, it does NOT qualify. If the behaviour can only be reached by entering the blocking interactive TUI (and thus cannot be exercised without hanging), report that as a finding rather than forcing an interactive launch.

tests.behaviour: `jobs create --action spawn` without `--prompt` is documented optional but server rejects it with an opaque error
steps: Run patch jobs create --cron "0 9 * * *" --action spawn --folder /tmp --name x --json against the live daemon (no --prompt)
Observe the response and exit code
Inspect `patch jobs create --help` which labels --prompt as 'Optional' and the usage error which lists only --cron + --action [+ --folder]
tests.expect: Either the prompt-less spawn job is created successfully (matching the 'Optional' docs), OR it fails with a specific actionable error that names the missing field (e.g. 'prompt is required for spawn jobs'). The current behaviour — exit 1 with the opaque {"error":"invalid_input"} that names no field while help says --prompt is Optional — does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: `jobs runs` and `jobs hooks` with a non-numeric --limit return a 500 Internal Server Error instead of clean client-side validation
steps: Run patch jobs runs <existing-jobId> --limit abc --json
Run patch jobs hooks <existing-jobId> --limit abc --json
Observe both responses and exit codes
tests.expect: Both commands reject the non-numeric --limit with a clear client-side validation error (e.g. '--limit must be a positive integer (got abc)') and exit 1, matching the `history` command's behaviour. Returning {"error":"Internal Server Error"} (an unhandled server 500) does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: `jobs runs --limit 0` and `--limit -5` are silently accepted and ignored rather than validated
steps: Run patch jobs runs <existing-jobId> --limit 0 --json
Run patch jobs runs <existing-jobId> --limit -5 --json
Compare the returned run count to an unlimited call
tests.expect: A zero or negative --limit is rejected with a clean validation error and exit 1 (consistent with history's '--limit must be a positive integer'). Silently ignoring the invalid limit and returning the full unfiltered run list with exit 0 does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: --limit validation messages are inconsistent across commands that accept --limit
steps: Run history/logs/jobs runs/jobs hooks/hooks tail each with --limit abc --json
Collect the error message, exit code, and whether validation is client- or server-side for each
tests.expect: All --limit-accepting commands reject non-numeric input with the SAME client-side validation message format and exit 1. The observed spread — history '--limit must be a positive integer (got abc)', logs 'bad --limit: abc', hooks tail silently returns {} exit 0, jobs runs/hooks 500 — does NOT qualify; a single consistent error contract across these commands is required.

tests.behaviour: `surfaces list` in human (non-JSON) mode prints nothing for an empty/any roster
steps: Run patch surfaces list (no --json) against the live daemon
Observe stdout
tests.expect: The command prints a human-readable result: either a surfaces table/rows or an explicit 'no connected surfaces' message, exit 0. Printing completely empty stdout (a blank screen with no feedback) does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: Special threads in `errored` status carry no error detail and are not surfaced by `doctor`
steps: Run patch threads list --json and identify any thread with status 'errored'
For each errored thread inspect its lastError field
Run patch doctor --json and read erroredChats
tests.expect: An errored thread either exposes a non-null lastError explaining the failure AND doctor's erroredChats count reflects errored threads, OR doctor exposes errored threads in a dedicated field. name: Web app — layout, sidebar, chat panel, routing, visual system

tasks.task:
The web SPA (packages/web) is the primary at-the-desk surface. It must faithfully implement the design in design/web-hi-fi.html using the tokens from design/hi-fi-tokens.css.

Verify and repair, testing the running app in a browser against a live server+daemon stack:

Visual system: cream #ebe7dc background, leaf green #4f7a3e accent, Fraunces italic display font, Inter body, JetBrains Mono for code/paths/timestamps. Paper/panel/raised surface colour tokens applied correctly. All radii, shadow levels, and colour states per spec. Light surface only — no dark mode for v1.

Layout: three columns — sidebar (280px default), main chat panel (fills remaining), editor (380px when shown). All column dividers are drag-resizable. State persists per-user (localStorage or server-stored). No top bar. Brand and connection dot in sidebar header.

Sidebar structure (top to bottom): brand row (patch wordmark in Fraunces italic + small connection dot, green=connected/orange=offline); Manager row (semibold, mic-btn hover-revealed); pinned chats section (standard badge + name + preview + always-visible pin marker + mic-btn); folders section (folder-head label in uppercase tracked ink-3 grey, chat rows ordered permission→working→done→read within each folder); Channels section (bordered, collapsed by default, Telegram + Speakers rows — both read-only, no composer, no mic-btn; Speakers row shows device pill e.g. '🎙 kitchen' when active); Archived row (no count, click expands with AI-powered search at top); bottom nav (Schedules + Settings rows with lucide icons, active state uses accent-tint background); +New chat button (full-width, dark fill, opens chat in main panel with no modal).

Status badges: working = flashing solid green dot (no ring); permission = orange dot + thick orange target ring; done/unread = green dot + thick green target ring; read = small grey ✓ tick + subtly greyed row text. Archived rows when expanded are NOT greyed (per spec).

Row tools: mic-btn hidden until row hover for regular chats, always visible for Manager and pinned rows. Pin marker always visible on pinned rows.

Chat lifecycle: opening a chat marks it read (unread → read). Auto-archive after exactly 3 hours of no new activity. New activity on archived chat → resumes as unread. Manual archive: on row hover, timestamp swaps to [archive] button. No duplicate archive control in chat header.

Main chat panel: role-coloured messages with markdown rendered and code blocks syntax-highlighted. Tool calls collapsed by default with one-line summary, click to expand full args + result. Inline unified diff view for file-edit tool results (read-only from stream). Permission prompts with Approve/Deny buttons inline (keyboard shortcuts 1/2/3 shown). Message context menu on right-click: retry / copy / inspect raw event. Composer: multiline text input, ⌘↵ to send, ⇧↵ for newline, placeholder text shows ⌘ ↵ to send hint.

Chat panel header: folder path (monospace, ink-3), chat name (Fraunces, slightly larger), 'waiting on you' orange pill with ! when permission state, ⋯ kebab menu (Pin chat/Unpin + View event log + Delete chat; hidden for special threads).

Routing: /chats/:chatId, /schedules, /schedules/:id, /schedules/new, /settings — all implemented as SPA routes with React Router v7.

Keyboard shortcuts: all 20+ shortcuts from the spec table must work (⌘?, ⌘K, ⌘/, ⌘N, ⌘⇧N, ⌘↑/⌘↓, ⌘⇧↑/⌘⇧↓, ⌘1, ⌘2, ⌘A, ⌘⇧A, ⌘J, ⌘P, ⌘', ⌘⇧', ⌘⇧E, ⌘↵, ⇧↵, 1/2/3 for permissions, Esc). Shortcut hints displayed next to buttons and in hover tooltips. ⌘? opens modal cheat-sheet.

Offline states: amber banner when server WS drops ('Reconnecting…'), composer disabled during disconnect, per-chat 'Daemon offline — messages queued' banner.

Archived search: AI-powered — query goes to a Claude Code session with access to full archived history. Do not build a custom search index.

State management: Zustand stores for chats, presence, voice, ui. TanStack Query for REST. WebSocket events update the cache directly.

name: Web app — Monaco diff editor and file browser

tasks.task:
The web app embeds Monaco for two distinct editor surfaces — the diff editor and the file browser. Both write via the same file.write wire event. The rule is to lean on Monaco's defaults; if a behaviour requires custom code beyond what Monaco offers, prefer dropping the behaviour over building it.

Verify and repair, testing against a live chat that has recently edited files:

Diff editor: opened by clicking a tool-call line in the chat stream or via ⌘'. Docked in the right rail at ~30% width by default. Shows unified diff only — no old/new/diff tabs, no side-by-side view. The diff is created with monaco.editor.createDiffEditor. Clicking any + or − line makes that line editable (the line becomes a visually distinct yellow editable box). Saving commits the file back to the daemon via a file.write wire event. ⤢ expands to a fullscreen takeover: sidebar and main panel hide, diff fills the page. A change-set rail on the left lists every file in the same edit for multi-file navigation. ⤢ again or Esc returns to docked. The diff editor is read-only when the chat's activity is running or awaiting-permission. Daemon enforces this: file.write events arriving when chat is not idle are rejected with a chat.error. Editor re-enables and becomes writable when activity returns to idle.

File browser: opened from [files] in the chat header or ⌘⇧'. Tree on the left (~280px), rooted at the chat's folder. Folders shown bold, expand/collapse. Green ● indicator next to filenames with pending changes (recent agent edit or unsaved user tweak). ⌘P opens fuzzy file search (input at top of tree). Editor on the right: full file content, line numbers, syntax highlighted, using monaco.editor.create. Read-only/writable rules are identical to the diff editor (chat must be idle to write). Meta strip above the editor has links: 'view diff vs HEAD' and 'view diff vs agent's last edit' — both flip the same file into the diff editor. Esc or × closes the file browser.

Both editors are scoped per-chat. There is no global 'browse all repos' surface. A chat is pinned to a folder; both editors are rooted there.

Test: open a chat, have the agent edit a file, click the tool-call line → diff editor opens in right rail with unified diff; click a + line → becomes editable; save → file changes on disk; ⤢ → fullscreen; Esc → back to docked; start a new agent turn → editor goes read-only; agent finishes → editor re-enables; open file browser → tree shows chat folder; ⌘P fuzzy search returns correct file; edit and save from file browser while chat is idle → succeeds; attempt edit while chat is running → rejected.

14-design-web.md ## File browser (entered from [files] in the chat header)

tests.behaviour: Clicking a tool-call line for an agent file edit opens a docked unified-diff editor in the right rail
steps: Open a chat where the agent has recently edited a file, and locate the tool-call line for that edit in the chat stream
Click that tool-call line and observe the editor surface that appears
Confirm it docks in the right rail (roughly a third of the panel width, not fullscreen) and that it presents a single unified diff of the changed file
tests.expect: PASS = a docked right-rail diff editor opens showing the file's changes as a single unified diff. Falsify if: it opens side-by-side or exposes old/new/diff view tabs; it opens fullscreen instead of docked; it opens the plain file (no +/- change markers); or nothing opens. Merely rendering a Monaco container with no diff content does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: The docked diff can also be opened via the keyboard shortcut for the most recent agent edit
steps: With a chat focused that has a recent agent edit and no editor open, invoke the keyboard shortcut documented for opening the diff of the last agent edit (discover it from the shortcuts spec/code rather than assuming the chord)
Observe whether the same docked unified-diff editor opens against the most recently edited file
tests.expect: PASS = the keyboard shortcut opens the docked unified diff for the most recent agent edit without any mouse click on the tool-call line. Falsify if the shortcut does nothing, opens the file browser instead, or opens a diff of the wrong (not most-recent) edit.

tests.behaviour: A changed line in the docked diff becomes inline-editable when clicked
steps: Open the docked diff for an agent edit so + and − lines are visible
Click a + or − line and observe whether that specific line turns into an editable input (the spec calls for a visually distinct yellow editable box)
Type a tweak into that line and confirm the edit is accepted in the editor before saving
tests.expect: PASS = clicking a changed line makes that line editable in place (visually distinguished, per spec yellow) and accepts typed input. Falsify if the whole diff is read-only with no per-line editing, if clicking a line does nothing, or if the editable affordance never appears. A globally-editable plain textarea is NOT the spec'd behaviour and does not qualify.

tests.behaviour: Saving an edit from the diff editor writes the change to the file on disk while the chat is idle
steps: With the chat in idle state, open the docked diff, make an inline edit to a changed line, and trigger Save
Independently inspect the actual file on disk in the chat's folder (read it from the filesystem, not from the UI) to confirm the saved content is present
Confirm the write travelled as the file.write wire event the spec mandates (the same event both editor surfaces use)
tests.expect: PASS = after Save, the on-disk file content reflects the user's tweak, and the save was carried by a file.write wire event. Falsify if the file on disk is unchanged, if the save only mutates in-memory UI state, or if it persists via some path other than the file.write wire event. A success toast / 200 alone does NOT qualify — the on-disk side-effect must be observed.

tests.behaviour: Expand toggles the docked diff into a fullscreen takeover with a multi-file change-set rail, and Esc returns to docked
steps: Open the docked diff for an edit that touched more than one file, then activate the expand control (⤢)
Confirm the sidebar and main chat panel hide and the diff fills the page, and that a change-set rail on the left lists every file in that same edit so you can navigate between them
Activate expand again (or press Esc) and confirm the view returns to the docked right-rail state
tests.expect: PASS = expand produces a fullscreen diff with sidebar/main hidden and a left change-set rail listing all files in the edit; selecting another file in the rail navigates to its diff; expand-again or Esc restores the docked layout. Falsify if expand only widens the rail without hiding sidebar/main, if no multi-file change-set rail appears for a multi-file edit, or if Esc/⤢ fails to return to docked.

tests.behaviour: The editor goes read-only while the chat is running or awaiting-permission and re-enables on return to idle
steps: Open the diff editor on an idle chat, then start a new agent turn so the chat enters running (and, if reachable, awaiting-permission) state
Observe whether the editor becomes read-only (no inline editing, save disabled/blocked) for the duration of the non-idle state
Let the agent turn finish so activity returns to idle, and confirm the editor becomes writable again
tests.expect: PASS = the editor is non-writable throughout running/awaiting-permission and becomes writable again once activity is idle. Falsify if the editor stays editable during running, if it never re-enables after returning to idle, or if read-only is only cosmetic (greyed) while edits still go through. Verifying against a chat that never leaves idle does NOT qualify — the running→idle transition must actually be exercised.

tests.behaviour: The daemon rejects a file.write that arrives while the chat is non-idle, emitting a chat.error
steps: Drive the chat into a non-idle (running or awaiting-permission) state, then cause a file.write wire event for a file in that chat to be sent to the daemon (discover the wire shape from the protocol spec / wire package rather than assuming fields)
Observe the daemon's response and inspect the target file on disk
Repeat the same write while the chat is idle to confirm the write is accepted then (control case)
tests.expect: PASS = while non-idle the write is refused with a chat.error and the file on disk is unchanged; while idle the equivalent write succeeds and the disk content changes. Falsify if a non-idle write silently succeeds (disk changes), if it is dropped with no chat.error surfaced, or if the daemon accepts it and relies only on the UI to block. Enforcement must be server/daemon-side, not merely a disabled button in the client.

tests.behaviour: The file browser opens from the chat header [files] control (and its shortcut), rooted at the chat's folder
steps: From a chat, open the file browser via the [files] control in the chat header (and separately confirm the documented file-browser shortcut opens the same surface — discover the chord, don't assume it)
Confirm a tree appears on the left (~280px) rooted at that chat's folder, with folders shown bold and expand/collapse working
Confirm there is no global 'browse all repos' affordance — the tree is scoped to this one chat's folder
tests.expect: PASS = the file browser opens rooted at the chat's own folder with a working bold-folder expand/collapse tree, openable from both [files] and its keyboard shortcut, with no cross-repo/global browse surface. Falsify if the tree is rooted somewhere other than the chat folder, if it exposes other repos, if folders don't expand, or if only one of the two entry points works.

tests.behaviour: Fuzzy file search in the file browser jumps to the correct file by partial name
steps: With the file browser open, invoke the go-to-file fuzzy search (input at the top of the tree; discover the shortcut from spec/code)
Type a partial/fuzzy fragment of a known file's name in the chat folder
Confirm the matching file is surfaced and selecting it opens that exact file in the right-hand editor
tests.expect: PASS = a fuzzy fragment surfaces the correct matching file and opening it loads that file's full content in the editor. Falsify if search returns no results for a valid fragment, returns the wrong file, or requires an exact full-path match (fuzzy/partial matching must work).

tests.behaviour: The file browser's right pane shows full syntax-highlighted file content with line numbers and respects idle-write rules
steps: Open a code file from the file-browser tree and confirm the right pane shows the complete file content with line numbers and syntax highlighting (Monaco standard editor)
With the chat idle, edit and save the file from the browser, then independently read the file on disk to confirm the change persisted via a file.write
Drive the chat non-idle and attempt to edit/save the same file from the browser, confirming the write is refused (same rule as the diff editor)
tests.expect: PASS = the right pane renders the full file with line numbers + highlighting; an idle save changes the on-disk file via file.write; a non-idle save is rejected. Falsify if content is truncated or unhighlighted, if an idle save doesn't reach disk, or if a non-idle save goes through. A 200/toast alone is not proof — the on-disk change (or its absence) must be observed.

tests.behaviour: A green pending-change indicator marks files with recent agent edits or unsaved user tweaks in the tree
steps: With a chat that has a recent agent edit to a known file, open the file browser and locate that file in the tree
Confirm a green ● indicator sits next to that filename, and that files with no pending change do not show it
Optionally make an unsaved user tweak to a clean file and confirm the indicator appears for it too
tests.expect: PASS = files with a recent agent edit (or unsaved user tweak) show the green ● and unchanged files do not. Falsify if the indicator is shown on every file indiscriminately, never shown despite a known pending change, or not green/not adjacent to the filename as specified.

tests.behaviour: The file browser meta strip can flip the current file into the diff editor against HEAD and against the agent's last edit
steps: Open a file in the file browser that has both a committed HEAD version and a recent agent edit
Use the meta-strip 'view diff vs HEAD' link and confirm the same file flips into the diff editor showing the diff against HEAD
Return and use 'view diff vs agent's last edit' and confirm it flips into the diff editor showing the diff against the agent's last edit (a different baseline)
tests.expect: PASS = both meta-strip links flip the same file into the diff editor, each against its respective baseline (HEAD vs agent's last edit), and the two diffs differ when the baselines differ. Falsify if either link is missing/inert, if both show the same baseline, or if they open a non-diff view.

tests.behaviour: The file browser closes with Esc or × and returns to the chat view
steps: Open the file browser from a chat, then press Esc and confirm the browser closes and the chat view is restored
Re-open the file browser and close it via the × control, confirming the same return-to-chat behaviour
tests.expect: PASS = both Esc and × close the file browser and restore the chat view. Falsify if either control fails to close it, if closing leaves the chat panel hidden/broken, or if Esc is swallowed and does nothing.

tests.behaviour: Clicking an agent file-edit tool-call line opens a diff that actually shows the agent's proposed change (old_string vs new_string), not an empty no-change diff
steps: Open the g3clean chat (timeline has an agent Edit of note.txt showing - hello world / + hello patch in the chat bubble)
Click the 'Edit note.txt' tool-call line to dock the diff editor
Read the original and modified sides of the Monaco diff editor
tests.expect: PASS = the diff editor's two sides differ, modified side shows the agent's proposed new_string 'hello patch' so the change is visible/approvable. FAIL = both sides render identical text ('hello world' on left AND right), i.e. the proposed edit is absent because the modified side was populated from unchanged on-disk content.

tests.behaviour: The docked (non-fullscreen) diff editor sizes to fill its rail width and does not clip line content
steps: At a ~1800px-wide window, open the g3clean chat and click an 'Edit note.txt' tool-call line to dock the diff editor (do NOT expand to fullscreen)
Measure the rendered width/position of the .monaco-diff-editor and its .view-lines vs the diff rail container, and read the visible line text
tests.expect: PASS = the Monaco diff editor fills the diff rail's content width and the line text 'hello world' is fully visible. FAIL = the diff editor renders at a tiny width (~150-180px) inside a much wider (~370px) rail leaving a large empty band, and the line text is clipped (e.g. shows 'hello wor').

tests.behaviour: The file browser's green pending-change dot reflects an actual pending change on disk, not merely that the agent referenced the file in chat
steps: Ensure note.txt and README.md on disk are at their committed/original content (no uncommitted change)
Open the g3clean chat, open the editor rail, switch to the Files tab
Inspect which files in the tree show the green pending-change dot
tests.expect: PASS = files with no actual on-disk change carry no green dot (dot only appears when the file genuinely differs from its baseline). FAIL = README.md and note.txt show green pending-change dots while their on-disk content is unchanged, because the dot is keyed off the agent having mentioned/edited the file in the chat timeline rather than a real disk diff.

tests.behaviour: Saving an inline edit in the docked diff editor surfaces explicit success feedback
steps: Open the g3clean chat, dock the diff editor on a file, click a changed line to make the modified side editable and type a change so Save enables
Click Save while the chat is idle
Observe the UI for a confirmation toast/indicator after the write
tests.expect: PASS = after a successful idle file.write the UI shows an explicit success confirmation (toast or equivalent). FAIL = Save commits the byte change to disk (verifiable by reading the file back) but the UI shows no success toast or visible confirmation, leaving the user unsure whether the write happened.

name: Web app — schedules, settings, menu-bar surface (Electron)

tasks.task:
The web app's schedules and settings pages plus the Electron desktop shell with menu-bar/tray surface.

Verify and repair, testing in a running Electron + browser session:

Schedules view (/schedules): job list showing trigger as human-readable text ('weekdays at 8:57', 'Todoist task tagged @claude') and action as verb (SKILL/PROMPT) + target. Matches design/web-lo-fi-schedules.html. Inline runs panel per job showing recent fires.

Job editor (/schedules/:id and /schedules/new): one form (no JSON tab, no wizard). Fields: trigger type select + config (cron expression shown, webhook secret+scheme, calendar calendarId+match, Todoist filter); JSONata filter shown raw (agent-generated, visible for inspection); action (two axes: spawn/message × skill/prompt — all four combinations valid); folder picker (for spawn); recipient chat picker (for message). /schedules/new wizard flow: pick trigger type → configure filter → configure action.

Settings (/settings): account section (email + disconnect action that deletes ~/.claude.json on daemon); linked devices (list with revoke per device); push tokens (registered Android devices); Telegram integration status (bot username, connected/not); Google OAuth status (connected/not, Calendar scope); daemon status (online/offline, last heartbeat) with add-daemon QR code shown when daemon not yet linked.

Manager incoming-call UX (web/desktop): when server triggers a Manager call via patch_call — app window raises to foreground if backgrounded; audible chime (short tone); overlay banner appears over the chat panel with Dismiss and Accept buttons. Accept → opens Manager voice session fullscreen takeover. Dismiss → events fall through to in-app inbox. No timer or countdown text on the banner.

Menu-bar surface (packages/desktop, Electron): tray icon always present in macOS menu bar. Click → 360px-wide dropdown panel: (1) Manager row with semibold text + phone icon (open voice call to Manager) + mic icon (tap-and-hold voice note to Manager); (2) compact chat list — five most-recent chats with status badges, name, folder + one-line preview, relative time, hover-revealed mic-btn — clicking a row launches full app focused on that chat; (3) Manager text input at bottom (placeholder 'Manager…', ⏎ fires as user turn into Manager). Dropdown is deliberately stripped — no connection-state header, no 'Open patch' link.

Global hotkeys (Electron globalShortcut): ⌃Space (hold) → voice-note overlay targeting Manager; ⌃⇧Space → voice call with Manager. These must work even when the full patch app window is not focused.

The menu-bar surface emits surface.heartbeat while the dropdown is open. No heartbeat when dropdown is closed (tray icon is OS chrome, not focus).

Test: open /schedules → verify all jobs visible with correct trigger labels; edit a job → changes saved and reflected on reload; /settings → disconnect and reconnect Claude account; Electron tray icon visible; click tray → dropdown appears with Manager row and chat list; ⌃Space globally opens voice-note overlay targeting Manager; Manager incoming call shows overlay with Accept/Dismiss; Accept opens voice session.
spec_sections: 14-design-web.md ## Menu bar surface (macOS, equivalents on Linux/Windows)

tests.behaviour: Schedules list renders each job's trigger as human-readable text and action as a verb + target
steps: Bring up the live web SPA against the running server+daemon and seed (via the CLI or daemon job-create path) at least one cron-triggered job and one Todoist-triggered job with distinct actions (a SKILL spawn and a PROMPT/MESSAGE).
Navigate to the schedules list view and read each row.

Confirm the trigger column shows natural language (e.g. 'weekdays at 8:57', 'Todoist task tagged @claude') and the action column shows the verb form (SKILL / PROMPT / MESSAGE) plus its target, not raw JSON/cron strings.
tests.expect: PASS = every seeded job appears with a humanized trigger label and a verb+target action label matching its underlying definition. Does NOT pass if rows show raw cron expressions / raw JSONata as the primary trigger text, if a job is missing from the list, or if the page only renders against hard-coded/mock data rather than the jobs actually present on the daemon (verify by adding a fresh job and reloading — it must appear).

tests.behaviour: Per-job inline runs panel shows recent fires for that job
steps: On the schedules surface, cause a job to actually fire at least once (trigger it through the real execution path so a run is recorded), then open that job's inline runs panel.
Read the runs panel contents.
Confirm a run entry corresponding to the real fire is shown.
tests.expect: PASS = the runs panel lists the genuinely-recorded fire(s) for that job, reflecting the run log written by the execution model. Does NOT pass if the panel is always empty, shows placeholder/static rows unrelated to actual fires, or never updates after a real run occurs.

tests.behaviour: Job editor is a single form (no JSON tab, no wizard) exposing trigger config, raw JSONata filter, four-way action, and folder/recipient pickers
steps: Open an existing job in the editor view.
Inspect the form: confirm there is no separate JSON/raw-payload tab and no multi-step wizard — one form.

Confirm it exposes a trigger-type select with its config (cron expression for cron, secret+scheme for webhook, calendarId+match for calendar, filter for Todoist), the JSONata filter shown raw/visible, an action control covering both axes (spawn vs message, skill vs prompt — all four combinations selectable), a folder picker shown for spawn actions, and a recipient chat picker shown for message actions.
tests.expect: PASS = the editor is a single form presenting all listed fields, the JSONata filter is visible verbatim, all four spawn/message × skill/prompt combinations are expressible, and folder vs recipient pickers appear according to spawn vs message. Does NOT pass if a JSON tab or wizard is present in the per-job editor, if the raw JSONata is hidden, or if any of the four action combinations cannot be selected.

tests.behaviour: Editing a job persists and survives reload
steps: Open an existing job, change a meaningful field (e.g. the action target or filter), and save.
Reload the page (or re-fetch from the server) and reopen the same job.
Independently confirm the change reached the daemon's job store (e.g. by reading the job back through the CLI/daemon job-get path).
tests.expect: PASS = the edited value is shown after reload AND is reflected in the job as stored on the daemon. Does NOT pass if the change only persists in client memory and reverts on reload, or if the UI reports success but the stored job is unchanged (a UI-only optimistic update is not proof).

tests.behaviour: New-job flow is a wizard: pick trigger type then configure filter then configure action
steps: Open the new-job creation flow.
Step through it and observe whether it guides the user through choosing a trigger type, then configuring the filter, then configuring the action.
Complete the flow to create a job and confirm the created job exists afterwards.
tests.expect: PASS = the new-job flow presents a trigger→filter→action wizard progression (distinct from the single-form per-job editor) and a completed run produces a real job persisted on the daemon. Does NOT pass if new-job is just the flat editor with no guided ordering, or if completing the wizard does not actually create a retrievable job.

tests.behaviour: Settings account section shows the connected Claude account email from daemon metadata
steps: With the real Claude daemon authenticated (OAuth, SDK_BACKEND=real), open the settings view.
Read the account/Claude-subscription section.
Confirm it shows a connected state with the account email sourced live from the daemon (~/.claude.json oauthAccount), not a hard-coded string.
tests.expect: PASS = settings shows the live connected account email reported by the daemon. Does NOT pass if it shows a placeholder/static email, shows 'not connected' while the daemon is in fact authenticated, or renders the email from front-end constants rather than the daemon-reported value.

tests.behaviour: Settings disconnect sends a real claude.disconnect to the daemon clearing the OAuth credential, and the surfaced state flips to not-connected
steps: From settings (connected state), invoke the Claude account disconnect action and confirm any confirmation prompt.
Observe the wire traffic / daemon behaviour: a disconnect event must reach the daemon and the daemon must report an unauthenticated/not-connected state back.
Confirm the settings UI then reflects the not-connected state with the re-auth instruction; then restore the credential to leave the stack usable for later tests.
tests.expect: PASS = disconnect triggers a real daemon-side credential-clear (observable as the daemon reporting unauthenticated / refusing queries) and the UI flips to not-connected. Does NOT pass if disconnect only toggles a UI flag with no event sent to the daemon, or if the daemon remains authenticated afterward (a green toast alone is not proof — the daemon state must actually change).

tests.behaviour: Settings shows linked devices with per-device revoke, push tokens, Telegram status, Google OAuth status, and daemon status
steps: Open settings and inspect the linked-devices, push-tokens, Telegram, Google OAuth, and daemon-status sections.

Confirm each section reflects live server/daemon state (a registered device is listed with a revoke control; daemon status shows online/offline + last heartbeat; Telegram and Google sections show connected/not-connected honestly).
Trigger a per-device revoke for a non-primary linked device and confirm the device is removed server-side.
tests.expect: PASS = all five sections are present and driven by live data, daemon-status reflects the actual daemon online state + a real heartbeat timestamp, and revoking a device actually removes it server-side. Does NOT pass if any section is static placeholder, if daemon status is hard-coded online, or if revoke does not actually invalidate/remove the device on the server.

tests.behaviour: Settings shows an add-daemon QR code when no daemon is linked
steps: Put the account into a state with no linked daemon (or inspect the code path that gates the QR), and open settings.
Confirm the daemon-status section surfaces an add-daemon QR code (with a real pairing nonce) in the not-yet-linked state, and that the QR is hidden once a daemon is linked.
Verify the QR encodes pairing data, not a placeholder image.
tests.expect: PASS = an add-daemon QR with a genuine pairing nonce appears precisely when no daemon is linked and is absent when one is linked. Does NOT pass if the QR is always shown/hidden regardless of daemon-link state, or if it is a static/decorative image with no pairing payload. If the no-daemon state cannot be reached on this dev stack, report that as a finding rather than marking pass.

tests.behaviour: Manager incoming-call overlay (server-triggered patch_call) raises the window, chimes once, and shows a banner with Dismiss/Accept and no timer
steps: With the app backgrounded/minimised, cause the server to trigger a Manager call via the real patch_call path.

Observe: the app window raises to foreground, one short chime plays, and a banner appears over the chat panel with a red 'MANAGER IS CALLING' header, green-ringed avatar, and two buttons Dismiss | Accept.
Confirm there is NO timer or countdown text on the banner.
tests.expect: PASS = a real server-initiated Manager call foregrounds the window, plays a single chime, and shows the Dismiss/Accept banner with no timer/countdown text. Does NOT pass if the banner only appears for a locally-faked event, if there is any countdown/timer text, or if the window does not raise when backgrounded.

tests.behaviour: Accepting a Manager incoming call opens the Manager voice session fullscreen; Dismiss lets events fall through to the in-app inbox
steps: From the incoming-call banner (from a real server-triggered call), press Accept and confirm a fullscreen Manager voice session takeover opens.
Trigger another real call and instead press Dismiss; confirm no voice session opens and the events fall through (the Manager chat receives/retains the activity in-app).
Check both buttons are wired to real session/inbox behaviour.
tests.expect: PASS = Accept opens the fullscreen Manager voice-call view and Dismiss routes the call through to the in-app inbox without a voice session. Does NOT pass if Accept merely closes the banner without opening a voice session, or if Dismiss drops the event entirely with no inbox fall-through.

tests.behaviour: Electron tray icon is always present and clicking it opens the 360px dropdown with Manager row, compact chat list, and Manager input
steps: Launch the Electron desktop shell (loading the web build) against the running stack.
Confirm a tray/menu-bar icon is present, then click it to open the dropdown.

Inspect the dropdown: ~360px wide, top Manager row with semibold text plus phone and mic icon buttons; a compact list of the five most-recent chats each with status badge, name, folder + one-line preview, relative time, and a hover-revealed mic button; and a bottom Manager text input with placeholder 'Manager…'. Confirm it is stripped — no connection-state header and no 'Open patch' link.
tests.expect: PASS = the tray icon exists and its dropdown contains the Manager row (with phone+mic), the compact recent-chats list with the listed per-row elements, and the Manager input, with no connection-state header or 'Open patch' link. Does NOT pass if the tray is absent, the dropdown omits any of the three regions, or it includes the deliberately-stripped chrome. Use the real Electron shell — a browser-only render of the route does not count for the tray-presence claim.

tests.behaviour: Clicking a chat row in the tray dropdown launches the full app focused on that chat; the Manager input fires a user turn into Manager
steps: From the open tray dropdown, click one of the chat rows and confirm the full patch app opens focused on that exact chat.

Type text into the Manager input and press Enter; confirm it is delivered as a user turn into the Manager chat (verify the turn lands in Manager's transcript on the daemon, not just cleared from the field).
tests.expect: PASS = clicking a row opens the full app on that chat, and submitting the Manager input produces a real user turn recorded in the Manager chat. Does NOT pass if the row click does nothing/opens the wrong chat, or if the Manager input clears without the turn actually reaching Manager.

tests.behaviour: Global hotkeys work OS-wide while the main app window is unfocused: hold opens a Manager voice-note overlay; the call chord opens a Manager voice call
steps: With the Electron shell running but its main window not focused (focus another app), discover the configured global voice-note chord and global voice-call chord (read the desktop main process to find them).
Trigger the voice-note hold chord and confirm the voice-note overlay appears targeting Manager even though the app window was not focused.
Trigger the voice-call chord and confirm a Manager voice call opens.
tests.expect: PASS = both global chords activate their respective Manager overlays while the main window is unfocused (proving they are OS-level globalShortcut bindings, not in-window key handlers), and both target Manager. Does NOT pass if the chords only work when the app window is focused, or if they target a chat other than Manager. If the host environment cannot deliver a true OS-global keystroke to the headless/emulated shell, report it as an environmentalBlocker naming the exact human action needed.

tests.behaviour: The menu-bar surface emits surface.heartbeat only while the dropdown is open, not while merely the tray icon is visible
steps: With the Electron shell running and the dropdown closed (tray icon visible), observe the server's surface presence / heartbeat signals attributable to the menu-bar surface over a window longer than the heartbeat interval.
Open the tray dropdown and observe again.
Close the dropdown and observe once more, correlating heartbeat presence with dropdown open/closed state.
tests.expect: PASS = surface.heartbeat from the menu-bar surface fires while the dropdown is open and stops when it is closed (tray-icon-only). Does NOT pass if heartbeats fire continuously regardless of dropdown state, or if no heartbeat ever fires while the dropdown is open. Observing a 'connected' socket alone is not proof — the recorded heartbeat cadence must track dropdown open/close.

tests.behaviour: Jobs CRUD is exercisable end-to-end via the daemon/CLI job tools (create, list, get, update, delete) backing the schedules surface
steps: Using the project CLI (pass --json) against the running stack, create a job, list jobs and confirm it appears, get it by id, update a field, and delete it.
After each mutation, independently confirm the change in the job store (re-list / re-get) and confirm the deleted job no longer appears.
Confirm the same jobs are the ones the web schedules view reads (consistency between CLI and UI surfaces).
tests.expect: PASS = create/list/get/update/delete each take real effect on the persisted job store and are mutually consistent, and the resulting jobs are the same set the schedules UI renders. Does NOT pass if any operation returns success without changing the store, if list/get are stale after a mutation, or if delete leaves the job retrievable.

name: Web app — voice input modes and overlays

tasks.task:
Voice input in the web app and desktop surface has three distinct modes, each with its own gesture and overlay UI. All three share the daemon's STT/TTS pipeline (covered in E1) — this group covers the surface-side UX and gesture handling.

Verify and repair, testing in browser and Electron against a running daemon:

Voice note overlay (mode 1 — single turn): triggered by press-and-hold of the chat row's mic-btn in the sidebar, OR the global ⌃Space hotkey (targets Manager). Two equivalent gestures: (a) press-and-hold → speak → release sends; (b) single tap → toggle mode (Superwhisper-style) → speak → ⏎ sends. Esc cancels without sending in either gesture. Overlay appearance: dark capsule pinned at bottom of screen, persistent across alt-tab. Contents: red ripple-mic glyph on left; active chat name + '· LISTENING' label; live STT transcript updating as user speaks (italic); waveform visualiser of incoming audio; subtle hint text '⏎ send · esc cancel' on right. Overlay does NOT steal focus from the underlying app. After send: audio committed as user turn with [voice • web] prefix; agent's reply routes per channel-aware rules (text in the surface).

Voice call overlay (mode 2 — persistent bidirectional): opened by tapping phone icon on Manager row in menu-bar dropdown, tapping sustained-voice control in a chat header, or accepting an agent-initiated incoming call. Daemon keeps audio WSS open; agent speaks via TTS, user replies, repeated until user ends call. Overlay: dark capsule with avatar + green ripple ring; 'ON CALL · <chat>' header; last spoken line in italic with speaker tag (MANAGER/KITCHEN/YOU); running call timer (e.g. '02:14'); mute-mic button; end-call (red phone) button. Persists across alt-tab. Focus-follow is active: navigating to a different chat mid-call routes next utterances there.

Focus-follow voice (mode 3 — chat header): clicking the chat-header voice control opens a tap-to-talk session for the current chat. This is a special case of mode 2.

All three overlays must be positioned identically (bottom-pinned capsule) and use the same component with different content. Reference: design/web-hi-fi-menubar.html frames 2 and 3.

Permission prompts during voice: when chat.permission_request arrives mid-voice-session, surface shows a banner with Approve/Deny plus a 'say yes / no' voice prompt. Spoken 'yes'/'no' goes through the Whisper path; daemon parses and emits chat.permission_response. Tap works too.

Manager incoming-call banner (specific to agent-initiated calls via patch_call): full-screen banner with red header strip 'MANAGER IS CALLING', green-ringed avatar, Dismiss and Accept buttons. Accept → voice-call overlay opens full-screen. No timer text. ↵ to accept as keyboard shortcut.

Barge-in visible to user: when user speaks while agent is responding, TTS audio cuts off immediately and a 'listening' state is shown — user should not experience a hung audio session.

Test: sidebar mic-btn press-and-hold → voice-note overlay appears, live transcript updates, release sends; toggle mode tap + ⏎ sends; Esc cancels; voice call from chat header → call overlay with timer; barge-in stops TTS; permission prompt during voice → speak 'yes' → approved; all overlays persist across alt-tab; focus-follow routes utterances to new chat after navigation.
