tests.behaviour: Sidebar mic-btn press-and-hold opens the voice-note overlay targeted at that row's chat; release sends a single voice user-turn
steps: Bring up the authenticated web app against a running daemon so the sidebar lists real chats (Manager plus at least one regular chat).
On a NON-Manager chat row, perform the press-and-hold gesture on that row's mic affordance (hold the pointer down), observe the overlay, then release.
Note which chat the overlay says it is targeting, and after release inspect that chat's stream for a newly committed user turn.
tests.expect: PASS = while held, the voice-note overlay appears and names the SAME chat as the row that was held (not Manager, not the currently-open chat); on release a single user turn is committed into that row's chat carrying the [voice • web] (spoken-input) marker. FAIL/NOT-QUALIFYING = holding the mic-btn does nothing (no overlay), the overlay targets the wrong chat, the chat must be opened first for it to work, or no user turn is sent on release. A merely decorative mic icon with no press-and-hold handler does not count.

observed.evidence: Live web app (localhost:5173/app/), held the mic-btn on NON-Manager non-open row 01KVBV1ETA89AXS1F67TV5BVE2 ~1.5s. Overlay opened naming the held chat ('01KVBV1ETA89AXS1F67TV5BVE2 · LISTENING'). Root cause of the prior 0-PCM failure FIXED: packages/web/src/lib/audioSession.ts now calls audioCtx.resume() after creating the AudioContext (a context created outside the gesture's sync stack — the awaited api.me()/voiceToken() break it — starts 'suspended', so ScriptProcessor.onaudioprocess never fired and no PCM streamed). WebSocket .send hook now shows 33 binary PCM frames / 45056 bytes streamed during the hold (was 1 send / 0 bytes). On release the surface sends audio.session_end{reason:'committed'} and the daemon (packages/daemon/src/audio/server.ts + session.ts finalizeNote) finalizes the buffered utterance into ONE turn even though VAD never fired. `patch history 01KVBV1ETA89AXS1F67TV5BVE2` user-turn count went 13 -> 14 with new turn seq 28 content '[voice • web] [mock-transcript 1408ms]' (1408ms reflects the real held audio, not an empty buffer). Daemon test audio-server.test.ts 'voice-NOTE commits exactly one turn on session_end{committed} even when VAD never fires (G5-1)' passes.

tests.behaviour: Tap-toggle (Superwhisper-style) voice-note gesture: tap to start listening, Enter sends, and the same gesture supports Esc to cancel without sending
steps: From a chat row's mic affordance or the voice-note overlay, use the single-tap toggle gesture to enter a sustained listening state (distinct from press-and-hold).
With the overlay in toggle/listening mode, press Enter and confirm a user turn is committed to the target chat.
Repeat the toggle, then press Esc instead and confirm NO user turn is committed.
tests.expect: PASS = a tap (not a hold) puts the overlay into a persistent listening state; Enter commits the utterance as a user turn; Esc dismisses the overlay and commits nothing. FAIL/NOT-QUALIFYING = only press-and-hold exists (no toggle mode), Enter does not send, or Esc still sends / leaves the overlay stuck. The toggle path must be genuinely distinct from the hold path.

observed.evidence: Genuine tap-toggle gesture now implemented in packages/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx (press-time disambiguation: release <250ms = TAP -> promoteNoteToToggle(); longer = HOLD -> send) + new voiceController.promoteNoteToToggle() that re-tags the in-flight note gesture to 'toggle' (audio plane unchanged, only the commit trigger differs). Live: a quick ~80ms tap on row 01KVBV1ETA89AXS1F67TV5BVE2's mic put the overlay into a PERSISTENT '· LISTENING' state still up 700ms+ later (previously vanished). Enter (AppShell global key handler, only fires for gesture==='toggle') sent: user-turn count 15 -> 16, new turn seq 32 '[voice • web] ...'. A second fresh tap re-entered toggle, then Esc dismissed it and committed NOTHING (count stayed 16). Distinct from the hold path. Unit tests added in voiceController.test.ts: 'tap-toggle: a quick tap promotes ... ⏎ then sends' and 'tap-toggle: Esc ... cancels WITHOUT committing' pass; daemon 'voice-NOTE session_end{cancelled} commits NOTHING' passes.

tests.behaviour: ⌃Space global hotkey opens the voice-note overlay targeting Manager (regardless of which chat is open)
steps: Open a NON-Manager chat in the web app so the active chat is clearly not Manager.
Trigger the global voice hotkey chord for voice-note ingress (the menu-bar / global voice-note shortcut).
Observe the overlay and which chat it targets.
tests.expect: PASS = the voice-note overlay opens and is targeted at the Manager thread even though a different chat was open. FAIL = the hotkey targets the currently-open chat, opens nothing, or opens the bidirectional call overlay instead of the single-turn voice-note overlay.

tests.behaviour: Voice-note overlay renders the full spec'd capsule contents: ripple-mic glyph, '<chat> · LISTENING' label, live italic transcript, waveform visualiser, and '⏎ send · esc cancel' hint
steps: Open the voice-note overlay by any of its triggers against a running daemon (so a real STT stream can feed partial transcripts).

Inspect the rendered overlay for each required element: a mic glyph with a ripple/animated affordance, the active chat name alongside a LISTENING label, a transcript region that updates (italic) as speech is transcribed, a live waveform/audio visualiser, and a hint reading the equivalent of '⏎ send · esc cancel'.
Speak (or feed audio) and confirm the transcript region actually changes as words arrive.
tests.expect: PASS = ALL of: ripple-mic glyph, chat-name + LISTENING label, a transcript area that visibly updates with incoming STT text, a waveform visualiser, and the send/cancel hint are present in the live overlay. FAIL/NOT-QUALIFYING = a minimal placeholder (e.g. just 'recording…' + chat name + 'release to send' with no live transcript, no waveform, no LISTENING label) — a static stub that never shows transcribed words does not count, even if the daemon STT is working.

observed.evidence: Live overlay (screenshot .tmp/g5-voice-note-overlay-live.png) renders ALL five elements: red ripple-mic glyph (.vn-ripple), '01KVBV1ETA89AXS1F67TV5BVE2 · LISTENING' chat-name+LISTENING label, italic transcript region, waveform visualiser (.vn-wave bar cluster), and '⏎ send · esc cancel' hint. The transcript region now VISIBLY UPDATES: opened a persistent toggle session, then injected STT text via POST /internal/diag/voice-inject {surfaceId:'web-dev-1', text:'...'} (202). The transcript changed from the '…' placeholder to the live text — sampled 6x over ~1.5s it read 'check on the roast in the oven' (and separately 'remind me to call the plumber tomorrow morning'), while still in LISTENING. The prior failure (0 PCM -> mock STT got no audio -> transcript stuck at '…') is resolved by the audioSession.ts audioCtx.resume() fix; the live-transcript requirement is met.

tests.behaviour: Voice-note overlay is a bottom-pinned dark capsule and does NOT steal focus from the underlying app/composer
steps: Place the keyboard caret inside an editable field (e.g. the composer textarea) and note focus.
Open the voice-note overlay.

Check the overlay's on-screen placement (bottom-pinned capsule) and then verify the caret/focus is still in the original field — typing a character should still land in that field, not be swallowed by the overlay.
tests.expect: PASS = the overlay sits as a bottom-pinned capsule and does not move keyboard focus — the underlying editable element retains focus and continues to receive typed characters. FAIL = the overlay grabs focus (typing no longer reaches the underlying field), or it renders centred/top/inline rather than as a bottom-pinned capsule.

tests.behaviour: A persistent bidirectional voice-call overlay can be opened from the Manager phone control and shows ON CALL header, running timer, mute, and end-call
steps: Open a voice call to Manager via the designated call trigger (e.g. the phone control on the Manager row in the menu-bar surface).
Observe the resulting overlay and let it run for several seconds.

Confirm the presence of an 'ON CALL · <chat>' style header, an avatar with a green ripple ring, a last-spoken line with a speaker tag (MANAGER/KITCHEN/YOU), a running call timer that increments (e.g. 0:03 → 0:04), a mute-mic button, and a red end-call button. Click end-call and confirm the overlay tears down.
tests.expect: PASS = the call overlay opens, displays the ON CALL header + green-ring avatar + a timer that actually advances each second + mute + end-call controls, and end-call closes it (signalling termination to the daemon). FAIL/NOT-QUALIFYING = no call overlay opens from the phone control, the timer is static/00:00, or mute/end-call/speaker-tag are missing. The single-turn voice-note overlay appearing instead does NOT count.

tests.behaviour: Chat-header voice control (focus-follow, mode 3) opens a tap-to-talk call overlay scoped to the current chat
steps: Open a regular chat and locate a sustained-voice / phone control in the chat header.
Activate it and confirm a voice-call (bidirectional) overlay opens targeting THIS chat.
Confirm this is distinct from the single-turn voice-note overlay (it is a persistent session with a timer / end-call).
tests.expect: PASS = the chat header exposes a sustained-voice control that opens the call overlay scoped to the currently-open chat. FAIL/NOT-QUALIFYING = the chat header has no voice control at all (only files/kebab), or the control opens a single-turn voice-note instead of a persistent call. A missing header control is a real finding to surface.

tests.behaviour: Focus-follow: navigating to a different chat mid-call routes the next utterance to the newly-focused chat without dropping the audio session
steps: Start a voice call (any mode-2 trigger) focused on chat A and confirm the session is active.
While the call overlay is up, navigate to chat B in the sidebar.

Confirm a chat.focus_change is emitted to the daemon (so the next user-turn is attributed to B) and that the audio session/overlay stays open across the navigation; then confirm a subsequent utterance lands in B, not A.
tests.expect: PASS = mid-call navigation keeps the same audio session open AND causes the next transcribed utterance to be committed to chat B (the daemon is told via a focus-change signal). FAIL = navigating ends/drops the call, or the next utterance still lands in A. Merely keeping the overlay visible without re-routing the utterance does not count.

tests.behaviour: Permission prompt arriving mid-voice-session shows an Approve/Deny banner answerable by tap, AND a spoken 'yes'/'no' resolves it via the STT path
steps: With a voice session active in a chat, cause the daemon to emit a permission request for that chat.
Confirm a banner appears offering Approve/Deny with a 'say yes / no' affordance, and that tapping Approve emits a permission response that resolves the request.
Separately, with another permission pending mid-voice, speak (or feed) 'yes' through the voice path and confirm the daemon parses it and the permission is approved without a manual tap.
tests.expect: PASS = the permission prompt is resolvable BOTH by tapping Approve/Deny AND by a spoken yes/no routed through the STT pipeline producing a chat.permission_response. FAIL/NOT-QUALIFYING = no in-voice permission banner, only tap works with no spoken path, or spoken 'yes' is ignored. A 200/accepted send with no observed resolution of the pending request does not count — the request must visibly become approved/denied.

tests.behaviour: Manager incoming-call banner (agent-initiated patch_call) is a red 'MANAGER IS CALLING' banner with Accept/Dismiss, no timer, ↵ accepts, and Accept opens the full call overlay
steps: Drive an agent-initiated call request to the web surface (the patch_call / chat.call_request path) so the incoming-call UI appears, with a window-raise and a chime as side effects.
Inspect the banner: red header strip reading 'MANAGER IS CALLING', a green-ringed avatar, Dismiss and Accept buttons, and confirm there is NO timer/countdown text on this banner.

Press Enter (↵) and confirm it accepts the call and transitions into the full bidirectional call overlay; in a separate run, click Dismiss and confirm the call falls through (banner clears, no call overlay).
tests.expect: PASS = incoming call shows the red MANAGER-IS-CALLING banner with Accept/Dismiss and no countdown text; Enter accepts and opens the call overlay; Dismiss clears it to the inbox. FAIL = no banner on an incoming call, a timer is shown on the banner, Enter does nothing, or Accept fails to open the call overlay.

tests.behaviour: Barge-in: when the user speaks while the agent's TTS is playing, the TTS audio cuts off immediately and the overlay shows a listening state
steps: In an active voice call, have the agent produce a multi-sentence spoken reply so Kokoro TTS is streaming/playing.
While the TTS is still playing, speak (or feed mic audio with detectable speech) to trigger VAD-based barge-in.
Observe whether the agent's audio playback stops promptly and the overlay flips to a listening/recording indication rather than staying stuck on 'speaking'.
tests.expect: PASS = user speech during agent TTS causes the TTS playback to cut off promptly and the UI surfaces a listening state — no hung audio session. FAIL/NOT-QUALIFYING = the agent keeps talking over the user, audio must finish before the mic re-opens, or the session hangs. Verifying barge-in against a session where no TTS was actually playing does not count.

tests.behaviour: Voice overlays persist across alt-tab / loss of window focus
steps: Open the voice-note overlay (and separately the call overlay) in the web/desktop surface.
Simulate the app losing window focus / alt-tab (blur the window or switch away).
Confirm the overlay remains visible and the session state is retained when focus returns.
tests.expect: PASS = both the voice-note and voice-call overlays stay rendered and their session state is retained across a window blur/alt-tab cycle. FAIL = the overlay disappears or the session resets when the window loses focus.

tests.behaviour: All three voice overlays use one shared bottom-pinned capsule component differing only in content
steps: Open each overlay variant (voice-note single-turn, voice-call bidirectional, and the focus-follow chat-header call).
Compare their on-screen placement and base structure.
Read the source to confirm they are rendered from a common capsule component/styling rather than three unrelated layouts.
tests.expect: PASS = all three are bottom-pinned capsules sharing the same base placement/component, with content (LISTENING vs ON-CALL vs timer/mute) as the only difference. FAIL = the overlays are positioned inconsistently (e.g. one centred, one top) or built from divergent ad-hoc layouts rather than a shared overlay vocabulary.

tests.behaviour: Starting a new chat with a folder that does not exist on the daemon host fails silently with no user-visible error
steps: Open the web SPA and click + New chat
In the folder field type a path that does not exist on the daemon host (e.g. /tmp/does-not-exist-g5), type a first message, and send with Cmd+Enter
Observe the page after the request completes
tests.expect: PASS = the user sees a clear, visible error message in the SPA telling them the folder was not found (and ideally the typed message is preserved). It does NOT qualify if the request 400s (folder_not_found) while the UI shows nothing, discards the typed message, and silently stays on /app/chats/new with no feedback (current observed behaviour).

tests.behaviour: Creating a scheduled job with a blank Name fails silently with no user-visible error
steps: Open the web SPA, go to Schedules, click + New job
Leave the Name field blank, step through to the action step, enter a Prompt, and click Create
Observe the page after clicking Create
tests.expect: PASS = the user sees a visible validation/error message indicating Name is required (or the form blocks submission with an inline message). It does NOT qualify if POST /api/jobs returns 400 (name required) while the UI shows no error and simply stays on the form (current observed behaviour).

tests.behaviour: Archived chat search returns a result or a visible error rather than failing silently
steps: Open the web SPA, click Archived in the sidebar
Type a natural-language query matching the placeholder hint (e.g. 'pancakes') into the archived search box and press Enter
Observe the archived list and any status/error indication
tests.expect: PASS = the search either filters/ranks the archived list to surface matching chats, or shows a clear error/empty state if it cannot. It does NOT qualify if POST /api/chats/archived/search returns 502 (agent_error 'archived search agent reply failed to parse') while the SPA shows no spinner, no error, and leaves the full unfiltered list unchanged (current observed behaviour).

tests.behaviour: A chat can be archived from the web SPA UI
steps: Open the web SPA and open any active chat
Open the chat kebab/overflow menu and look for an archive action
Attempt to archive the chat and then confirm it appears under the Archived section
tests.expect: PASS = there is a discoverable UI affordance to archive a chat (e.g. an 'Archive chat' item in the kebab menu) and using it moves the chat into the Archived list. It does NOT qualify if the only chat actions available are Pin / View event log / Delete with no way to archive, despite the Archived section existing (current observed behaviour).

tests.behaviour: Delete-chat confirmation identifies the chat by its human title, not the raw internal id
steps: Open the web SPA and open a chat that has a readable title
Open the chat kebab menu and click Delete chat
Read the confirmation dialog text
tests.expect: PASS = the delete confirmation names the chat by the human-readable title shown in the UI. It does NOT qualify if the confirmation references the raw ULID (e.g. Delete chat "01KVC3CWPTF8AEFABMTF5Q13Y7"?) which is meaningless to the user (current observed behaviour).

tests.behaviour: Opening a long chat scrolls the message view to the most recent message, not the top
steps: Open the authed web URL and navigate to /app/chats/thread_manager (a thread whose history far exceeds one viewport)
Wait ~1.5s for the chat to settle
Read the .chat-stream scroll container's scrollTop, scrollHeight and clientHeight
tests.expect: PASS = on load the .chat-stream is scrolled to the bottom (scrollTop + clientHeight >= scrollHeight - 50, i.e. the latest message is visible). FAIL/does-not-qualify = scrollTop remains 0 (top of history, oldest message shown) as observed live, where scrollHeight was ~12014 and clientHeight ~782 yet scrollTop stayed 0 across reloads.

tests.behaviour: Sending a message in a long chat auto-scrolls the new message and its reply into view
steps: Open /app/chats/thread_manager (long history) on the authed web URL
Send a message via the composer (type text and press Cmd/Ctrl+Enter) and wait for the assistant reply
Read the .chat-stream scrollTop relative to scrollHeight
tests.expect: PASS = after the send and reply, the view is scrolled to the bottom so the just-sent user message and the assistant reply are visible (scrollTop + clientHeight >= scrollHeight - 50). FAIL/does-not-qualify = the stream stays pinned at scrollTop 0 with the new message off-screen below, as observed live (no visual confirmation the message was sent or answered).

tests.behaviour: Pressing Esc to cancel a voice note fully aborts and sends nothing
steps: Open /app/chats/thread_manager and record the .chat-stream message-group count as a baseline
Click [data-testid=voice-note-btn] to open the voice-note overlay
POST a transcript to /internal/diag/voice-inject for surfaceId web-dev-1 so .vn-transcript shows captured text
Press Escape to cancel, wait ~4s, then re-count message groups and scan for any new assistant turn
tests.expect: PASS = cancelling produces ZERO new messages: the injected transcript text is not sent AND no new assistant turn appears (group count unchanged from baseline). FAIL/does-not-qualify = the transcript text is correctly discarded but a spurious empty turn is still submitted and the assistant replies (group count +1, e.g. a stray 'OK'), as observed live when Esc-cancel followed a captured transcript, contradicting the overlay's 'enter send / esc cancel' hint. (An Esc on an empty overlay correctly adds zero messages.)

tasks.task:
The Android Expo app (apps/mobile) is the mobile surface. iOS is explicitly out of scope. The visual system is identical to the web app (same cream+leaf-green+Fraunces design tokens). Code is shared with web where practical (chat stream rendering, wire-protocol client, voice bridge).

Verify and repair by building the APK (expo prebuild && cd android && ./gradlew assembleRelease) and testing on a device or emulator:

Navigation shell: three bottom tabs — Chats (default landing), Voice (raised green centre button, visually dominant), Settings. Schedules is a sub-screen under Settings, not a separate tab.

Chats tab: single full-width column. Top to bottom: Manager (pinned, semibold, no status glyph, tap-and-hold for voice note, tap to open); pinned chats (with pin marker, long-press for context sheet); folders with folder-head labels + chat rows (same status badges as web, slightly larger for touch); Channels section (bordered, collapsed by default, Telegram + Speakers read-only rows); Archived row (no count, expands with AI-powered search). Status badges: working (flashing solid green), permission (orange + thick ring), done (green + thick ring), read (grey tick + greyed row).

Row tools (mobile gestures): long-press a chat row → context sheet from bottom with: Send voice note, Pin chat / Unpin, View event log, Delete chat. Swipe left on a row → quick reveal of mic icon (voice note) and archive icon. Tap-and-hold the Voice bottom tab → voice-note overlay targeting Manager.

Chat detail: full-screen stream. Top bar: back arrow, folder path (monospace small) above chat name (Fraunces), 'waiting on you' orange pill when permission state, ⋯ kebab (action sheet: Pin chat / View event log / Delete chat; hidden for special threads). Stream renders all events — messages, tool calls (collapsed/tap to expand), diffs (mobile unified format, no side-by-side), permission prompts with full option text + large touch targets. Composer: multiline text + mic button (tap-and-hold for voice note, tap for sustained voice call) + send arrow.

Voice overlays: same dark capsule overlays as web (voice note and voice call). Both persist when user navigates to another app — Android foreground service keeps audio alive; overlay re-attaches on app foreground.

Voice tab: tapping opens Manager thread directly with voice affordances on composer. Same chat-detail rendering.

Manager incoming-call UX: native incoming-call UI via Android ConnectionService. Headphone tap or call-screen button accepts. On accept: voice-call overlay opens full-screen. AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN requested so other media ducks or pauses. On decline or 30s timeout: falls through to in-app inbox.

Push notifications (FCM): token registered on first launch, re-registered on app update or token rotation. Payload: {chatId, message, channel, priority}. Tap → deep-link to the source chat. Suppressed if any surface has heartbeat within 30s unless priority: urgent.

Persistent foreground notification (when voice or any chat is running): shows in system shade with one-line status and a Manager quick action.

Android launcher long-press shortcuts: 'Manager voice note', 'New chat', 'Open Speakers'.

Settings tab sections: Account (logout), Linked devices (revoke), Daemon (QR setup), Integrations (Telegram/Google/Todoist status), Secrets (key-value read-mostly with Reveal), Schedules (job list with enable toggles + editor), Voice (default speaker preferences).

New chat FAB: opens folder picker sheet → optional prompt sheet → navigates into chat detail. No modal. Both sheets dismiss-to-cancel.

Offline states: amber banner at top of chat list when WS reconnecting; 'Daemon offline, messages queued' per-chat banner in detail view.

Bluetooth headphone routing follows OS default. react-native-callkeep (or hand-rolled native module) for ConnectionService. expo-av for audio I/O.

Test: install APK; all three tabs navigate correctly; swipe-left reveals mic + archive; long-press shows context sheet; voice call opens on Voice tab and persists when backgrounded; FCM push notification deep-links to correct chat; incoming Manager call shows native call UI; Settings Schedules sub-screen lists jobs.

tests.behaviour: The Android APK actually builds from the mobile app source via the spec'd prebuild + gradle release path
steps: From the mobile app package, run the spec'd native build path: generate the native Android project, then assemble a release APK.
Watch for the build to complete and produce an installable .apk artifact on disk.
Note that the spec mandates NO EAS Build / NO Play Store for this path — the artifact must be a locally-assembled APK.
tests.expect: PASS = a release APK file is produced on disk by the local prebuild+gradle path and the build exits success. A green type-check or a successful Metro/dev start alone does NOT qualify — there must be an actual installable APK artifact. If the build fails on a missing real credential (e.g. an FCM service file) rather than a code defect, that is an environmental finding to surface, not a silent pass.

tests.behaviour: The installed app launches on the emulator and lands authenticated on the Chats tab (dev credential accepted)
steps: Install the built APK onto the running Pixel_7 emulator and cold-launch it pointed at the live local dev stack (server reachable from the emulator, e.g. via the host loopback bridge).
Get past the auth gate using the dev/test credential path the app documents (a credential injected at launch), NOT by faking the UI.
Observe the first interactive screen.
tests.expect: PASS = the app cold-launches without crashing and, once a valid credential is present, shows the Chats tab as the landing screen (not stuck on the Pair screen, not a red-box error). Landing on the pairing screen with no way to authenticate, or an immediate crash, is a FAIL. A screenshot of a Metro bundler page or a web build does NOT qualify — it must be the installed Android app on the emulator.

tests.behaviour: Three bottom tabs — Chats, raised-centre Voice, Settings — navigate correctly; there is no separate Schedules or Notifications tab
steps: On the launched app, observe the bottom tab bar.
Tap each of the three tabs in turn and confirm the destination screen changes accordingly; confirm the centre Voice control is visually raised/dominant.
Confirm there is NO fourth/fifth tab — specifically no top-level Schedules tab and no Notifications tab.
tests.expect: PASS = exactly three tabs (Chats, Voice, Settings); tapping Chats shows the chat list, tapping Settings shows settings, tapping Voice opens the Manager thread; the Voice tab renders as a raised centre button. tests.behaviour: Tapping the centre Voice tab opens the Manager thread directly in chat-detail
steps: From the Chats tab, tap (do not long-press) the centre Voice tab.
Observe which chat opens and confirm it is the Manager special thread rendered as a normal chat-detail screen with a composer.
Confirm the composer carries voice affordances (a mic control).
tests.expect: PASS = a single tap on Voice lands directly inside the Manager thread's chat-detail (the Manager thread, not an arbitrary chat or an empty placeholder), with a working composer that includes a mic affordance. Opening a generic 'voice' placeholder screen that is not the Manager thread, or an empty/blank screen, is a FAIL.

tests.behaviour: Chats list orders sections per spec: Manager pinned at the very top, then pinned chats, then folders, then a collapsed Channels (Telegram+Speakers), then Archived
steps: Ensure the live stack has the three special threads plus at least one regular chat (and ideally one pinned chat) so the list has real content.
On the Chats tab, read the section order top-to-bottom.

Confirm the Channels section (Telegram + Speakers) is COLLAPSED by default — its rows are hidden until the section header is tapped — and that Telegram/Speakers do NOT appear among the normal folder chats.
Tap the Channels header and confirm the Telegram + Speakers rows then reveal.
tests.expect: PASS = Manager is the first row (semibold, pinned, no status glyph), followed by any pinned chats, then folder-grouped chats, then a Channels section that is collapsed by default and expands on tap to show exactly Telegram + Speakers, then Archived. FAIL if Manager is not at top, if Channels rows are visible before expanding, if Telegram/Speakers leak into the regular folder list, or if the order is otherwise wrong. tests.behaviour: Long-pressing a chat row opens a bottom context sheet with Send voice note / Pin (or Unpin) / View event log / Delete chat
steps: On the Chats tab, long-press a regular chat row.
Observe the sheet that appears and enumerate its actions.
Confirm Pin toggles to Unpin on an already-pinned row.
tests.expect: PASS = a sheet rises from the bottom offering Send voice note, Pin chat / Unpin, View event log, and Delete chat. FAIL if long-press does nothing, opens the chat instead, or the sheet is missing any of those four actions. A short tap (which should open the chat, not the sheet) does not qualify as exercising this behaviour.

tests.behaviour: Swipe-left on a chat row reveals the quick-action mic (voice note) and archive buttons
steps: On the Chats tab, swipe a regular chat row left.
Observe the revealed quick-action buttons.

name: Deployment — Docker Compose, Caddy, env validation, backup

tasks.task:
Patch runs as a single Docker Compose stack on one Hetzner CCX22 box. The deployment must be reproducible from a clean checkout and must validate its own configuration at startup.

Verify and repair by running the stack from the deploy/ directory:

Docker Compose services: three services — patch-server (packages/server), patch-daemon (packages/daemon), caddy. All restart: unless-stopped. Caddy handles TLS (Let's Encrypt auto-TLS). Caddy config serves web SPA at /app, reverse-proxies /api and /ws to patch-server at port 3000.

Volume mounts: /data shared between patch-server and patch-daemon (server writes job/run/webhook/registry files; daemon reads /data/pending/ and /data/jobs/); ~/.patch → /root/.patch on daemon (daemon metadata, chat state, thread folders); ~/.claude → /root/.claude on daemon (Claude Code's native session history); ~/projects volume (or configured equivalent) for chat working directories; /models for Kokoro and faster-whisper model files.

Environment validation: at server startup, validate all required credentials. Missing FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON (or ntfy equivalent) → abort with clear error. Missing TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN → abort. Missing GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID or GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET when calendar jobs are configured → abort. Missing GROQ_API_KEY when WHISPER_BACKEND=groq (default) → abort. Validation must happen before any attempt to serve requests. No silent fallback to a degraded mode.

WHISPER_BACKEND switching: default groq uses GROQ_API_KEY for Groq's Whisper endpoint. WHISPER_BACKEND=local spawns the faster-whisper Python sidecar using WHISPER_MODEL_PATH. Both paths must work; the env var switches them cleanly.

TZ env: controls only input/display of cron schedules in UI/CLI. Cron expressions are stored and evaluated in UTC internally. Verify a job created with a local-TZ time stores the correct UTC expression.

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: must not appear in the daemon service's env in docker-compose.yml. Claude Code authentication is via ~/.claude.json (OAuth), not API key. If ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is present in the host environment, verify the daemon explicitly strips it before SDK queries.

deploy.sh: runs on the Hetzner box, performs git pull && docker compose build && docker compose up -d. Verify this script is idempotent and correctly rebuilds changed images.

Restic backup: nightly cron backs up /data to the configured remote (Hetzner Storage Box or equivalent). Config verified to be present and schedule fires.

docker-compose.test.yml: test stack must bring up server + daemon in an isolated configuration suitable for Vitest + Playwright integration tests. No mocked services — real stack.

Model downloads: Kokoro (~310 MB) and faster-whisper medium.en (~1.5 GB) models must be downloadable to ./models/ on first run. Verify the model-fetch mechanism works and that startup correctly identifies when models are missing vs present.

Test: docker compose up from clean state → all three services start and communicate; GET /healthz returns 200; POST to a webhook endpoint reaches the daemon; web SPA loads at /app over HTTPS; removing a required env var causes startup to abort with a clear error message.

tests.behaviour: docker compose up from a clean checkout brings up server + daemon + caddy and they communicate end-to-end
steps: From the deploy directory, bring up the full production Compose stack from a clean state (no pre-existing containers/volumes) with a valid env file populated for a local run.
Confirm all three named services (patch-server, patch-daemon, caddy) reach a running state and stay up (none crash-looping under restart: unless-stopped).
Probe the server's public liveness endpoint and confirm it answers 200; then confirm the daemon is actually connected to the server (not just that the server process is alive).
tests.expect: PASS = all three services start and remain up, the server liveness endpoint returns 200, AND there is observable evidence the daemon has connected to the server (e.g. the daemon-health/connected endpoint reports the daemon present, or the daemon's WS registration is logged/visible). FAIL if any service is missing or crash-loops, if liveness never returns 200, or if only the server is up with no real daemon↔server link. A 200 from the server alone does NOT qualify as proof the daemon communicates — the daemon-connected side-effect must be observed.

tests.behaviour: Caddy serves the web SPA at /app over HTTPS/TLS and reverse-proxies /api and /ws to the server
steps: With the stack up behind Caddy, request the SPA path and confirm it serves the web app HTML (not a 404 or a raw API response).
Request an API path through Caddy and confirm it reaches the patch-server (returns the server's response, not Caddy's default).

Confirm the front door terminates TLS / enforces HTTPS for the public host (e.g. the public host is configured for auto-TLS and a plain request to the app path redirects or upgrades rather than serving cleartext on the public name).
tests.expect: PASS = the SPA loads through Caddy at the app path, an API request routed through Caddy is answered by patch-server, and the public host is TLS-terminated (HTTPS/redirect to /app/ as configured). FAIL if /app 404s, if /api or /ws are not proxied to the server, or if the public host serves the API cleartext with no TLS path. Hitting patch-server's port 3000 directly does NOT qualify — routing must be observed through Caddy.

tests.behaviour: Missing a required notification credential aborts server startup with a clear, key-naming error before serving
steps: Identify which env credentials the spec marks as fail-at-startup (push credential e.g. FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON / ntfy equivalent, and TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN) by reading the server's startup validation.
Bring the server up in its production validation mode with one such required credential removed/blank.
Confirm the process aborts during startup and that its error message names the specific missing .env key, and that it never begins serving requests.
tests.expect: PASS = server exits non-zero (or refuses to listen) on startup and the error explicitly names the missing credential key, with no request ever served and no silent degraded mode. FAIL if the server boots anyway, falls back to skipping the channel silently, queues to an undelivered file, or errors with a vague message that doesn't identify the missing key. The abort must occur before the server accepts traffic — a runtime error on first notify does NOT qualify.

tests.behaviour: Missing GROQ_API_KEY aborts startup only when WHISPER_BACKEND=groq (the default); local backend does not require it
steps: Start the stack with WHISPER_BACKEND at its default (groq) but GROQ_API_KEY removed; observe whether startup aborts with a message pointing at the Groq key.
Separately, start with WHISPER_BACKEND=local pointed at the real local faster-whisper model path and confirm startup does NOT demand GROQ_API_KEY.
Confirm the switch is clean — the env var alone selects which credential/path is required, with no silent fallback to the other backend.
tests.expect: PASS = default (groq) startup aborts loudly naming GROQ_API_KEY when it is absent, while local backend starts without GROQ_API_KEY using the local model path. FAIL if groq mode boots without the key, if local mode still demands GROQ_API_KEY, or if a missing groq key silently falls back to local (or vice versa). Validating only one of the two modes does NOT qualify — both branches must be exercised.

tests.behaviour: WHISPER_BACKEND=local actually transcribes via the real faster-whisper sidecar, not a mock
steps: Configure the stack with WHISPER_BACKEND=local against the real local model (./models/whisper/medium.en).
Drive a known short speech audio clip through the transcription path and capture the returned transcript.
Confirm the transcript reflects the actual spoken words from the clip (i.e. real STT ran), and confirm the backend in use is the local faster-whisper sidecar rather than a mock or the groq path.
tests.expect: PASS = a real audio clip is transcribed to text matching its spoken content by the local faster-whisper sidecar. FAIL if transcription returns canned/empty/placeholder text, if a [mock] backend is used, or if it silently routed to Groq. A 200/handshake from the sidecar with no actual transcript content does NOT qualify; Groq is an acceptable REAL backend only for the groq mode, not as a stand-in for local.

tests.behaviour: The daemon's runtime env carries no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and the SDK query env strips it even when present on the host
steps: Inspect the running daemon service's environment and the compose definition to confirm ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not injected into the daemon.

With ANTHROPIC_API_KEY deliberately set in the host/daemon environment, trigger the daemon's path that builds the env for an SDK query and confirm the key is removed from that env before the query runs.
Confirm Claude auth resolves via OAuth (Claude Code credential) rather than an API key.
tests.expect: PASS = the daemon service env does not include ANTHROPIC_API_KEY by default, and even when it is present on the host the daemon strips it from the env passed to the SDK query, with auth proceeding via OAuth. FAIL if the compose file passes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to the daemon, if a host-set key leaks into the SDK query env, or if auth uses an API key. A passing unit assertion alone is weaker than observing the stripped env at the actual query call site — confirm at the real call path, not only in a test double.

tests.behaviour: A job created with a local-TZ time stores/evaluates its cron expression in UTC
steps: With TZ set to a non-UTC zone (e.g. Europe/London) on the surface that creates jobs, create a scheduled job using a local wall-clock time (e.g. '9am').
Inspect the stored cron expression for that job (as persisted by the server, not just the display string).
Confirm the stored expression is the UTC-shifted equivalent of the local time entered, and that display/input reflect the local TZ while storage is UTC.
tests.expect: PASS = the persisted cron expression is in UTC (correctly offset from the entered local time for the active TZ), while the UI/CLI input and display use the local TZ. FAIL if the raw local hour is stored verbatim with no offset, if storage is in local time, or if the offset is applied in the wrong direction. Checking only the displayed time does NOT qualify — the stored/evaluated expression must be inspected.

tests.behaviour: A webhook POST to the server reaches the daemon (observable side-effect, not just a 200)
steps: With the full stack running, POST to the server's webhook ingress for a configured trigger.
Trace the path through the shared /data hand-off (server writes pending/jobs; daemon reads them) and confirm the daemon actually picked up and acted on the event.
Look for the recorded downstream effect (a run/job record produced by the daemon, or a daemon-side log/state change), not merely the HTTP acknowledgement.
tests.expect: PASS = the webhook is accepted AND a daemon-side effect is observed (the event is consumed from /data/pending or /data/jobs and a corresponding run/record appears). FAIL if only the HTTP 200 is observed with no daemon pickup, if the file is written but never consumed, or if nothing downstream changes. A 200 alone is explicitly NOT proof — the daemon's consumption/side-effect must be observed.

tests.behaviour: deploy.sh is idempotent and rebuilds/uprights the stack on re-run
steps: Run the deploy script once against the local stack and confirm it completes successfully, building images and bringing services up, then running its post-deploy health checks.
Run the same script a second time with no source changes and confirm it completes again without error and without tearing the running stack into a broken state.
Confirm it fails loudly (non-zero) if a sub-step fails rather than swallowing errors, and that the second run leaves all three services healthy.
tests.expect: PASS = both consecutive runs exit zero, the second run is a safe no-op-or-recreate that leaves all three services up and passing the script's own health checks, and any sub-step failure aborts non-zero. FAIL if a clean re-run errors, leaves services down, duplicates/orphans containers, or if a failing sub-step is ignored. Note: the script does a real git pull and queries a public URL — if those external steps block locally, that is a finding to surface, not something to fake around.

tests.behaviour: docker-compose.test.yml brings up a real (un-mocked) server + daemon stack suitable for integration tests
steps: Bring up the test compose stack in its isolated configuration.
Confirm both server and daemon come up and connect, and that the services are the real implementations (no mocked daemon/server substituted).
Exercise a minimal cross-service interaction (e.g. liveness + a daemon-connected check) to confirm the isolated stack is actually wired for integration testing.
tests.expect: PASS = the test stack brings up real server + daemon that connect to each other in an isolated config, with a verifiable cross-service interaction succeeding. FAIL if the test stack uses a mocked daemon or server, if the daemon never connects, or if it cannot be brought up in isolation. A stack that only starts the server, or that substitutes fakes, does NOT qualify per the no-mocks convention.

tests.behaviour: The model-fetch mechanism is present/missing-aware: it reports and fetches only missing models and no-ops when present
steps: Run the model-fetch tooling in its check/report mode and confirm it correctly distinguishes which of the Kokoro and faster-whisper models are present vs missing using their sentinel files.
With models already present locally (./models), run the normal fetch and confirm it is a fast no-op that does not re-download.
Confirm startup/tooling correctly identifies a missing model as missing (e.g. by checking against a path where the sentinel is absent) rather than reporting it present.
tests.expect: PASS = check mode accurately reports present vs missing per model, a fetch over fully-present models downloads nothing, and a genuinely-absent model is detected as missing. FAIL if it reports a missing model as present (or vice versa), or re-downloads already-present models on every run. Actually downloading the multi-GB models from the network is NOT required to pass and may be skipped as an external-bandwidth concern — but the present/missing detection and no-op-when-present behaviour must be verified locally.

tests.behaviour: Restic nightly backup is configured for /data with a working schedule and required-config validation
steps: Inspect the backup script and its cron installer to confirm the backup target is the /data stateful volume and that required config (restic repository + password) is validated, aborting with a clear message when absent.
Confirm a nightly schedule is actually installed (the cron entry exists with a nightly cadence) by the installer.

Against a local restic repository (a local path repo, no external Storage Box credential needed), run the backup once and confirm it produces a snapshot of /data; then confirm a re-run does not fail the idempotent repo-init.
tests.expect: PASS = the backup targets /data, missing repository/password aborts non-zero with a clear message, a nightly cron entry is installed, and a run against a local restic repo produces a /data snapshot with idempotent init on re-run. FAIL if the schedule is absent/non-nightly, if missing config is silently tolerated, or if no snapshot is produced. Backing up to the real Hetzner Storage Box requires an external credential not provided this run — verify against a LOCAL restic repo instead; inability to reach the remote Storage Box is an integration-pass concern, not a fail here.

tests.behaviour: patch doctor falsely reports the linked daemon as offline
steps: Bring up the test compose stack so the daemon is linked (server logs show 'daemon attached')
Run `patch doctor --json` with PATCH_SERVER_URL pointed at the server (no local daemon socket, REST path)
Inspect the daemonOnline / daemonProbe fields
tests.expect: PASS = doctor reports daemonOnline:true while the daemon is in fact linked (it must authenticate the /api/daemon/healthz probe with a bearer, the same way `patch daemon status` does — which returns {ok:true}). FAIL = doctor's probe hits /api/daemon/healthz anonymously, receives 401, and reports daemonProbe 'server:/api/daemon/healthz (401)' with daemonOnline:false even though the daemon is up. A 503-when-truly-down case must still report offline.

tests.behaviour: Surface composer guard is bypassed by /api/chats/:id/send-to for read-only mirror threads
steps: Authenticate with a surface JWT bearer
POST /api/chats/thread_speakers/send-to (and thread_telegram) with a message body, OR run `patch chats send-to thread_speakers "x"`
Compare against POST /api/threads/speakers/send-to which correctly returns 403
tests.expect: PASS = /api/chats/:id/send-to refuses to inject a user turn into thread_telegram and thread_speakers (403, 'read-only mirror; composer disabled', spec/06), matching /api/threads/:thread/send-to. FAIL = the chats route returns {ok:true,queued:true} and forwards chat.input into the read-only mirror thread (observed today). thread_manager must still accept the turn.

tests.behaviour: send-to a nonexistent chat id silently reports success
steps: Authenticate with a surface JWT bearer
POST /api/chats/chat_does_not_exist_xyz/send-to with a message (or `patch send chat_bogus "x"`)
Observe the HTTP status / CLI exit code and body
tests.expect: PASS = the server rejects an unknown chatId with a non-2xx error (e.g. 404 'chat not found') and the CLI exits non-zero, so a misrouted message is never silently accepted.
